A fund-manager network spreads sourcing and specialist judgement beyond the state balance sheet.
preconditions: A public investment institution with a mandate, capital and governance that can tolerate long time horizons
Private fund managers and co-investors able to select, price and support high-growth firms
A pipeline of investable companies and follow-on capital so an anchor commitment can compound rather than stand alone
pattern.travelled: Public venture catalysts travel when they crowd in capable private managers and preserve commercial decision-making; a state fund without deal flow, follow-on finance or disciplined governance can become a subsidy ledger rather than a capital market.

records.title: ICURe, from university research to spinouts
records.claim: UK Research and Innovation's ICURe impact report says spinout companies from the programme secured £326 million in investment funding and created more than 1,400 jobs from 2014 onward, after research teams were trained and funded to test markets before deciding whether to spin out.

metric.name: Investment secured by ICURe spinouts

secondMetric.name: Jobs created by ICURe spinouts

source.publisher: UK Research and Innovation, ICURe impact report

records.limits: The impact report's cumulative investment and job figures cover teams supported by ICURe and do not show the full spinout population, survival, profitability, quality of jobs, counterfactual or the programme's independent contribution. They are programme impact estimates, not a national spinout rate or a guarantee that every participating discovery should become a company.

pattern.mechanism: ICURe gives research teams funding, coaching and a disciplined market-discovery period in which they conduct more than 100 customer interviews before a university-backed go/no-go decision. Teams advised to spin out can then apply for follow-on funding, turning technology-transfer work into an investable proposition rather than treating a patent as a company.
preconditions: Universities and research institutes with discoveries, translational staff and authority to support commercial routes
Researchers willing to test a problem with users and founders able to lead a company after the discovery phase
Follow-on grants, investors and technology-transfer offices that can carry a validated opportunity beyond the programme
pattern.travelled: Spinout pipelines travel when market discovery, founder formation and follow-on capital are designed as one chain; a grant or patent alone does not create the commercial capabilities and decisions needed for a durable firm.

records.title: Ramp Up, PROCOMER's export-readiness programme
records.claim: Costa Rica's export agency PROCOMER reported that 40 SMEs graduated from its 16-week Ramp Up 2024 programme, delivered with INA and the Sistema de Banca para el Desarrollo, bringing the number of firms benefiting since the programme began in 2021 to 175.

metric.name: SMEs graduating from Ramp Up 2024

secondMetric.name: SMEs benefiting since launch

source.publisher: PROCOMER, Ramp Up 2024 export-capability programme

records.limits: Graduation and reach counts show programme delivery, not verified export growth, new markets, product diversification, export survival or causal impact. PROCOMER describes the firms as strengthening export capability; the source does not establish that all graduates exported or that the programme changed Costa Rica's aggregate concentration.

pattern.mechanism: PROCOMER, the national training institute and a development bank combine practical training in finance, strategy, governance and sustainability with export-market connections. The package builds the organisational routines and compliance readiness that small firms need before an overseas buyer or distributor can become repeat business.
preconditions: An export agency that can identify firms, broker market access and coordinate services rather than offering disconnected workshops
SMEs with a product, management time and enough operational capacity to act on finance, quality and sustainability work
Training, development finance and buyer or standards networks that remain available after graduation
pattern.travelled: Export-readiness programmes travel when capability-building is tied to real market links and finance; a course certificate without buyer validation, working capital or standards support rarely diversifies exports by itself.

records.title: Cooperative Research Centres programme
records.claim: Australia's Department of Industry reported that its Cooperative Research Centres portfolio facilitated 304 businesses establishing research-focused collaborations in 2023–24, across 114 CRC and 190 CRC Projects partners, above the year's target of 248.

metric.name: Businesses establishing research-focused collaborations

secondMetric.name: Portfolio target

source.publisher: Australian Department of Industry, Science and Resources, Annual Report 2023–24

records.limits: The partner count measures collaborations facilitated through grant agreements, not completed research, commercialisation, additionality or university-only links. It is an administrative portfolio measure whose reporting and retrospective calculations can change, and partners include research organisations and community bodies alongside universities and businesses.

pattern.mechanism: Australia funds industry-led research centres for three to ten years and shorter CRC Projects for up to three years, giving firms and researchers a shared programme, matching resources and a governance structure for applied work. The long and short formats let a mature collaboration and a focused translation project coexist.
preconditions: Universities, research organisations and firms able to define a problem together and commit staff or cash
A competitive public grant process with independent assessment and enough duration for trust and technical work to accumulate
A centre-level governance and intellectual-property framework that can turn joint research into adoption or further investment
pattern.travelled: University–industry centres travel when public grants buy durable shared capacity and firms own a consequential problem; short networking schemes without governance, matching effort or a path to adoption produce thinner ties.

records.title: Singapore's national ICT-skills measurement and baseline
records.claim: Singapore's Department of Statistics ICT-skills table reports 99.0% in the total row for residents aged 16–74 in 2025, while 55.2% could use a basic arithmetic formula in a spreadsheet; the government uses the series to track SDG 4.4.1 and its Digital Skills for Life framework.

metric.name: Residents with an ICT skill in the total row

secondMetric.name: Basic spreadsheet arithmetic skill

source.publisher: Singapore Department of Statistics, annual ICT-skills dataset (IMDA source)

records.limits: The table records task-specific self-reported or survey-derived skills for Singapore residents, not independently tested proficiency, workplace transfer or equal access. The age base changed from residents aged 15 and above in 2016–2020 to ages 16–74 from 2021, and a high total can hide weak performance on harder tasks such as spreadsheet work.

pattern.mechanism: Singapore pairs a recurring skills measurement with a public baseline framework, Digital Skills for Life, and targeted support such as Seniors Go Digital. The combination makes digital capability a population service obligation rather than a one-off computer course, while the task rows reveal where basic access still masks deeper gaps.
preconditions: A statistical agency and digital ministry able to repeat a common task taxonomy and publish the results
Universal connectivity and trusted public services that give adults reasons to practise digital tasks in daily life
Accessible coaching, devices and safety guidance for older and lower-income residents who are least likely to learn informally
pattern.travelled: Digital-skills programmes travel when measurement, everyday use and targeted help reinforce one another; connectivity statistics alone can conceal a population that still cannot complete consequential tasks.

records.title: Singapore Courts' case-clearance discipline
records.claim: Singapore's State Courts disposed of 21,816 civil cases against 20,358 filings in 2023, a 107% civil clearance rate; its Community Justice and Tribunals courts recorded a 99% clearance rate in the same year.

metric.name: State Courts civil-case clearance rate

secondMetric.name: Community Justice and Tribunals clearance rate

source.publisher: Singapore Judiciary, Caseload statistics 2023

records.limits: Clearance is disposals divided by filings in the same year, so it can exceed 100% when courts work through earlier stock; it does not show timeliness, fairness, legal-aid access, enforcement or the quality of decisions. The Singapore figures cover court workloads and are not a comparable cross-country civil-justice index without harmonised case definitions.

pattern.mechanism: Singapore Courts publish workload by court and case type, set clearance as a management measure and combine procedural reform with specialised tribunals and dispute-resolution pathways. The public series makes backlogs visible while the court system can shift suitable disputes into faster channels without pretending that every case is the same.
preconditions: A judiciary with reliable case-management data and authority to redesign procedure across court tiers
Registries, judges, mediators and tribunals that can route cases by complexity rather than use one queue for all disputes
A public accountability norm that treats unresolved caseload as an operational problem while protecting judicial independence
pattern.travelled: Court-clearance management travels when administrative data, triage and dispute resolution reduce stock without turning speed into the only definition of justice.

records.title: France's long-term unemployment decline
records.claim: France's national statistics office Insee reported that people unemployed for at least one year represented 23.3% of all unemployed people in 2024, while the long-term unemployment rate was 1.7% of the active population, down from 3.1% in 2015.

metric.name: Long-term unemployed as share of all unemployed

secondMetric.name: Long-term unemployment rate

source.publisher: Insee, Evolution du chômage / Employment Survey 2024

records.limits: The figures describe labour-market duration, not the causes of unemployment, the quality of re-employment or whether training and employment services produced the decline. Insee's household-survey definitions and population scope matter, and a low long-term share can coexist with high short-term churn or discouraged workers outside the unemployment measure.

pattern.mechanism: France's employment system combines unemployment insurance, employment-service counselling and targeted training or hiring support, helping some jobseekers move through the labour market before unemployment becomes persistent. The falling long-term rate is an outcome to investigate, not proof that one programme caused it.
preconditions: A labour-force survey and employment-service records that distinguish duration consistently
Income support and active labour-market services that preserve contact with jobseekers while they search
Employers, training providers and regional intermediaries able to convert counselling into credible vacancies or skill transitions
pattern.travelled: Long-term-unemployment reductions travel when income support, matching and skills services are connected to real employer demand; a falling rate can otherwise reflect exits from the labour force rather than successful re-employment.

records.title: Federal funding gaps and the 2019 shutdown
records.claim: The Congressional Research Service records 20 federal funding-gap shutdowns with at least one full day between FY1977 and FY2019, including the 35-day partial shutdown from 21 December 2018 to 25 January 2019, the longest in the period it surveys.

metric.name: Longest partial federal shutdown

secondMetric.name: Funding-gap shutdowns with at least one full day

source.publisher: Congressional Research Service, Past Government Shutdowns: Key Resources

records.limits: Shutdown duration and frequency are institutional consequences that can reflect constitutional rules, divided government and bargaining strategy, not a direct measure of public attitudes or latent polarisation. The CRS series ends in FY2019 for this historical resource, and a shutdown's operational cost varies with which agencies lose budget authority.

pattern.mechanism: The US appropriations process allows a lapse in budget authority to stop or furlough parts of the federal government, turning unresolved political conflict into an interruption of administration. Continuing resolutions and contingency plans soften the shock but do not remove the incentive or the coordination cost of brinkmanship.
preconditions: Separated institutions in which the executive and legislature can block or condition annual appropriations
A legal shutdown rule that makes funding lapses administratively real rather than automatically extending the prior budget
Political parties willing to use public-service disruption as leverage, plus contingency systems that limit but cannot eliminate the damage
pattern.travelled: Funding-gap reversals travel as a warning: constitutional checks need a credible continuity mechanism, or polarised bargaining can turn a disagreement into a measurable loss of state capacity.

records.title: Chave Móvel Digital and Portugal's digital identity layer
records.claim: Portugal's digital-government platform reported 4.4 million active Chave Móvel Digital credentials and 141 million authentications by 23 October 2025, with 490 entities using Autenticação.gov.

metric.name: Active Chave Móvel Digital credentials

secondMetric.name: Authentications through Autenticação.gov

source.publisher: Portugal Digital / ARTE, Identidade Digital statistics

records.limits: These are administrative adoption and usage totals, not measures of service quality, inclusion, authentication success, fraud or trust. An active credential is not necessarily a unique active person, and the government platform reports the totals itself; the figures do not show whether citizens can complete the services they authenticate for.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal made one state-certified mobile credential usable for authentication and signatures across public services and participating private services, so each new service can reuse an existing identity rather than build a separate account system.
preconditions: A trusted civil-identity register and a legal basis for remote signatures
Interoperable authentication APIs and agencies willing to adopt one national gateway
Registration, recovery and offline support for people who cannot rely on a smartphone
pattern.travelled: A shared digital identity travels when legal recognition, cross-agency interoperability and assisted access travel with the credential; a login count alone can hide exclusion or weak service completion.

records.title: Portugal's CoLAB applied-research network
records.claim: Portugal's Agência Nacional de Inovação reported 41 recognized Collaborative Laboratories (CoLABs), and its 2024 innovation report recorded 639 highly qualified staff contracted by CoLABs, 32 percent of them PhDs.

metric.name: Recognized Collaborative Laboratories

secondMetric.name: Highly qualified staff contracted by CoLABs

source.publisher: Agência Nacional de Inovação, Relatório Nacional de Inovação 2024

records.limits: The network and staffing totals show institutional reach, not research quality, business adoption, additionality or durable jobs. CoLABs are separate private non-profit entities and report through the programme; the figures do not cover every university-industry link or establish that public recognition caused the reported staffing.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal gives mission-led applied-research organisations a formal recognition and monitoring route, then combines public base or competitive funding with industry-facing agendas so researchers have an institution whose job is to carry work across the university-business boundary.
preconditions: Universities and firms willing to share researchers, facilities and intellectual-property arrangements
A public agency able to recognize, monitor and renew organisations against research and transfer agendas
Stable mixed funding so an applied laboratory can pursue long projects without becoming a consultancy only
pattern.travelled: The CoLAB form travels when recognition is tied to an accountable applied mission and real employer or industry demand; a list of centres without shared incentives does not create technology transfer.

records.title: Programa Qualifica and Portugal's adult-learning network
records.claim: Portugal's ANQEP reported 1,025,569 cumulative Qualifica registrations by December 2023; 90 percent received a training or recognition, validation and certification referral, and 510,113 registrants obtained some certification.

metric.name: Cumulative Qualifica registrations

secondMetric.name: Registrants receiving a certification

source.publisher: ANQEP, Plano de Atividades 2024

records.limits: These are cumulative programme reach and certification totals, not an annual participation rate, completion quality, learning gain or employment and wage effect. The count can include partial certifications and administrative registrations, and it does not identify how many participants would have qualified without Qualifica; ANQEP reports the programme's own administrative data.

pattern.mechanism: A national network of Centros Qualifica gives adults a common entry point for counselling, recognition and validation of prior learning (RVCC), formal training and a portable qualification record, linking fragmented providers to a visible pathway.
preconditions: Local centres with counsellors and assessors able to validate work-based learning
A qualification framework and records that employers and schools can understand
Funding and referral links to training providers, employment services and employers
pattern.travelled: Adult-learning systems travel when advice, prior-learning recognition and funded courses form one route; registrations without follow-through can otherwise become a throughput statistic rather than capability.

records.title: Portugal Ventures, a public venture-capital bridge
records.claim: Portugal Ventures, the public venture-capital company in the Banco Português de Fomento group, reports €233.2 million invested in 256 new companies since 2012 and €283 million under management.

metric.name: Invested since launch

secondMetric.name: New companies backed since launch

source.publisher: Portugal Ventures, institutional performance figures

records.limits: These are company-reported cumulative portfolio figures, not venture-capital investment as a share of GDP, additionality, exits, survival, jobs or a counterfactual. The homepage does not give a full reference-year methodology, and the totals can include private co-investment effects as well as Portugal Ventures' own capital.

pattern.mechanism: A state-backed investor supplies pre-seed, seed and Series A capital, often alongside private investors, using staged minority investments and portfolio support to bridge companies that are too early for ordinary bank finance.
preconditions: A pipeline of founders and research-derived firms large enough to fill investment rounds
Investment professionals with authority to make commercial decisions inside a public mandate
Follow-on private capital and exit markets so public money can recycle rather than become permanent subsidy
pattern.travelled: Public venture capital travels when it crowds in follow-on investors and accepts portfolio risk transparently; a state fund that only replaces missing private money can preserve firms without building a market.

records.title: Novas Oportunidades, and the qualification-policy interruption
records.claim: ANQEP's national review records 1,568,490 adult enrolments in Novas Oportunidades between 2006 and July 2011; after the initiative's peak and a period of disinvestment, Portugal launched Qualifica in 2017 and rebuilt a network of more than 300 Centros Qualifica.

metric.name: Adult enrolments in Novas Oportunidades

secondMetric.name: Centros Qualifica in the replacement network

source.publisher: ANQEP, Plano Nacional de Literacia de Adultos

records.limits: Enrolment is a reach measure, not completed learning, quality, labour-market effect or value for money. The review's 1.57 million figure covers a high-activity period, while the later 300-plus-centre figure describes the replacement network rather than retained Novas Oportunidades capacity; the record evidences interruption and rebuilding, not a causal estimate of the policy's return.

pattern.mechanism: Novas Oportunidades scaled adult qualification through recognition and validation of prior learning (RVCC), adult education and training (EFA) routes and a national delivery network; when political and fiscal support receded, the infrastructure contracted and a successor programme had to rebuild entry points.
preconditions: A national qualification framework that can turn work experience into recognized credits
Local centres, assessors and training providers able to process large cohorts
Long-horizon funding and cross-party continuity, because adult-learning capacity is slow to rebuild after a stop
pattern.travelled: The interruption travels as a warning: mass adult-learning systems need continuity and credible standards, or a high-enrolment push can leave a capability gap when the delivery network is withdrawn.

records.title: Orçamento Participativo Portugal
records.claim: Portugal's first national participatory-budget cycle drew almost 80,000 votes and committed €3.18 million to winning projects, which were written into the 2018 state budget.

metric.name: Votes cast in the first OPP cycle (approximately)

secondMetric.name: Investment committed to winning projects

source.publisher: Presidência e Modernização Administrativa, OPP 2017 results

records.limits: A single cycle's votes do not establish sustained civic participation, representativeness, deliberative quality or whether every winning project was delivered on time. The government announcement reports the programme's own participation and budget totals, and the national cycle was later redesigned rather than becoming a stable annual measure of citizen voice.

pattern.mechanism: The central government opened a national proposal and voting platform, reserved a defined slice of the state budget, and promised to place winning projects in departmental budgets so participation could produce a visible delivery rather than only consultation.
preconditions: A public budget line that can be set aside before proposals are voted on
A technical process for screening proposals without removing the final choice from citizens
Departments and regions willing to implement projects they did not originate
pattern.travelled: Participatory budgeting travels when a vote is linked to a protected implementation route; a platform without a budget, screening and delivery owner produces participation theatre.

records.title: Empresa na Hora and the one-stop company registry
records.claim: Portugal's IRN reports 369,447 societies created through Empresa na Hora over its first 20 years; the service is available at more than 200 posts and averages 41 minutes from formation to registration.

metric.name: Companies created through Empresa na Hora

secondMetric.name: Average service time

source.publisher: Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado, Empresa na Hora 20-year results

records.limits: The throughput and elapsed-time figures measure a standard incorporation route, not the full time or cost of becoming operational, survival, access for less standard firms or the quality of subsequent regulation. IRN reports its own service and cumulative count, and the average can hide variation by company type, name choice and whether applicants arrive prepared.

pattern.mechanism: A single state counter combines name approval, incorporation and registration, passes the record between public services electronically and later extends the same workflow online, converting a multi-agency legal process into one accountable transaction.
preconditions: A shared company register and legal authority for one service to complete several acts
Interoperable registries and pre-approved names that remove sequential approvals
A fallback for complex companies and foreign founders whose cases do not fit the standard route
pattern.travelled: One-stop registries travel when back-office data sharing is real and the simple route is measured end to end; a fast counter that leaves tax, licensing and beneficial-ownership steps separate only moves the queue.

records.title: Plano de Recuperação e Resiliência delivery governance
records.claim: Portugal's PRR barometer recorded €21.9 billion across 121 investments and 43 reforms, with €14.43 billion paid to beneficiaries by 27 August 2026.

metric.name: PRR funds paid

secondMetric.name: Investments in the plan

source.publisher: Portal Mais Transparência / Estrutura de Missão Recuperar Portugal, PRR barometer

records.limits: Funds paid, investment counts and reform counts are programme inputs and milestones, not completed infrastructure, cost and schedule performance or long-run outcomes. The plan is EU-funded and centrally coordinated but executed through many ministries and beneficiaries; the barometer's aggregate totals cannot attribute results to one delivery unit or show which projects will remain useful after the funding window closes.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal bound a large cross-government investment programme to a reform-and-milestone schedule, central monitoring and payment requests, while leaving implementation to ministries, public bodies, firms and local beneficiaries. The financing contract creates a common delivery clock across otherwise separate projects.
preconditions: A central authority able to consolidate milestones and submit evidence for payment
Project owners with procurement, co-financing and reporting capacity
A transparent public dashboard that exposes slippage and reallocations before the deadline
pattern.travelled: Milestone-funded national plans travel when the payment gate is credible and project owners can report comparable evidence; a large envelope without a delivery spine becomes a catalogue of announcements.

records.title: Sistema de Gestão Integrada de Fogos Rurais
records.claim: Portugal's integrated rural-fire system reported 85 of 97 national-action projects in progress and 48 percent cumulative execution in 2024; €638 million was spent that year, with 55 percent on prevention, even as 137,651 hectares burned.

metric.name: National-action projects in progress

secondMetric.name: SGIFR expenditure

source.publisher: Agência para a Gestão Integrada de Fogos Rurais, SGIFR annual results 2024

records.limits: Projects in progress and spending are capacity measures, not proof that communities are safe; the 2024 burned-area and mortality figures show the residual risk plainly. Annual fire outcomes also depend on weather, land use and ignition behaviour, so the record cannot identify the causal contribution of coordination, prevention or suppression spending.

pattern.mechanism: After the 2017 fires, Portugal replaced a mainly suppression-led model with a cross-government system linking prevention, landscape management, preparedness, suppression and recovery, coordinated by AGIF and reported against a national action programme.
preconditions: A permanent coordinating agency with authority to aggregate eleven ministries and dozens of entities
Shared risk data and annual reporting that make prevention visible beside emergency response
Municipalities, landowners and emergency services able to turn national priorities into local work
pattern.travelled: Integrated fire governance travels when prevention budgets, operational command and landowner incentives share one accountable plan; extra firefighting capacity alone does not change the hazard.

records.title: Simplex and LabX, a standing simplification-and-experimentation loop
records.claim: AMA's 2022 activity report records 48 Simplex administrative-simplification measures, 24 PRR and modernisation milestones executed, and 62 innovation, participation and simplification activities across the agency's portfolio.

metric.name: Simplex measures in the 2022 edition

secondMetric.name: Innovation, participation and simplification activities

source.publisher: Agência para a Modernização Administrativa, Activity Report 2022

records.limits: Counting measures and workshops shows an administrative improvement pipeline, not reduced burden, faster case resolution or better user outcomes. AMA reports its own activity, and combining the recurring Simplex programme with LabX experiments hides which initiatives reached routine service delivery and which remained pilots. AMA has since been renamed ARTE and no longer hosts the report, so the record cites a Wayback Machine snapshot (6 May 2024) of the original PDF.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal pairs a rolling political simplification agenda with a public-sector innovation lab: Simplex names and tracks changes, while LabX researches user needs, co-creates prototypes and tests service redesign before agencies adopt it.
preconditions: A centre of government able to convene ministries around cross-cutting administrative changes
A safe experimental space with permission to test services with citizens and officials
Owners and monitoring that carry a successful prototype into law, procurement and routine operations
pattern.travelled: A simplification-and-experimentation loop travels when pilots have a route into the rulebook and service budget; a lab without an adoption owner becomes a workshop catalogue.

records.title: Programa Nacional de Vacinação and seasonal immunisation
records.claim: Portugal's DGS reported 86 percent immunisation of eligible infants in the first RSV campaign, 98–99 percent first-year coverage for the universal childhood schedule, and nearly four million seasonal vaccines administered in 2024–2025.

metric.name: Eligible infants immunised against RSV

secondMetric.name: Universal-schedule first-year coverage (lower bound)

source.publisher: Direção-Geral da Saúde, Programa Nacional de Vacinação annual results

records.limits: Coverage is not the same as immunity, health impact or equal access, and the rounded seasonal-dose total is not a count of unique people. These figures mainly cover Portugal Continental and the DGS reports the programme's administrative data; high routine coverage can coexist with gaps in older groups, migrants or particular municipalities.

pattern.mechanism: A national schedule, procurement and registry make routine childhood vaccination a standing service, while seasonal campaigns add new products, broaden delivery through pharmacies and publish coverage by age and municipality so the system can adapt to a changing respiratory threat.
preconditions: A trusted national immunisation schedule and supply chain
Primary-care, hospital and pharmacy channels able to share records and deliver at scale
Local surveillance and public communication that can identify pockets of low coverage
pattern.travelled: Vaccination systems travel when routine infrastructure can absorb a new campaign quickly and coverage is visible below the national average; a one-off mass purchase without records and delivery channels fades when the emergency does.

records.title: STAYAWAY COVID, a contact-tracing app suspended after the emergency
records.claim: Portugal launched the voluntary STAYAWAY COVID exposure-notification app on 1 September 2020; the European Commission's case study records more than 3.2 million downloads and says the app was later suspended.

metric.name: App downloads (more than)

source.publisher: European Commission, Digital Contact Tracing Study: Portugal case

records.limits: Downloads do not show active use, the share of infected people entering test codes, alerts delivered or epidemiological effect. The voluntary, privacy-preserving design depended on test-result integration and public trust, and suspension after the emergency means the adoption peak was not a durable surveillance capability.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal combined a national health authority with research and technology partners to deploy an anonymous Bluetooth exposure-notification app quickly, using voluntary adoption rather than a centralised movement database.
preconditions: A trusted health authority able to validate positive-test codes
Interoperable laboratory and notification systems that make an alert actionable
Public trust in privacy safeguards and a clear endpoint when the emergency passes
pattern.travelled: Digital emergency tools travel when they connect to routine health workflows and retain legitimacy after the crisis; a download surge without operational integration is easy to dismantle.

records.title: e.escola, a national laptop-and-broadband push
records.claim: The European Commission's eSchool case study records more than 1.3 million people requesting laptops and broadband through Portugal's e.escola programme and more than one million laptops delivered in its first two years; the Portuguese government suspended the programme in 2011.

metric.name: People requesting laptops and broadband (more than)

secondMetric.name: Laptops delivered in the first two years (more than)

source.publisher: European Commission Interoperable Europe, eSchool Programme (Portugal case)

records.limits: Device distribution measures access, not sustained use, adult or student digital competence, learning outcomes or affordability after the subsidy. The scale figures come from the programme case study, while the suspension is recorded in a Portuguese government archive; the partnership and outstanding state payments also complicate any simple claim of a completed success.

pattern.mechanism: The state used a dedicated fund and mobile-operator partnership to put subsidised laptops and broadband into the hands of students, teachers and adult trainees, using schools and private partners for decentralised delivery.
preconditions: A mechanism to target subsidies across students, teachers and low-income households
Private network operators able to supply devices and connectivity at national scale
Maintenance, training and replacement funding that lasts beyond the initial hardware handout
pattern.travelled: Device-and-connectivity programmes travel when skills support, maintenance and a durable funding model accompany procurement; a rapid hardware push can leave a capability gap when the subsidy is withdrawn.

records.title: PLANAPP and REPLAN, a centre-of-government foresight network
records.claim: Portugal's PLANAPP operates as a Centre of Government body for evidence-based foresight, planning, monitoring, evaluation and impact analysis; its REPLAN network lists five multisectoral team remits and held its inaugural meeting on 23 November 2022.

metric.name: Named multisectoral REPLAN team remits

source.publisher: PLANAPP, REPLAN presentation

records.limits: The five is a count of named remits on PLANAPP's presentation page, not a verified staffing or output measure; the same page describes the teams as four before listing five. The record therefore evidences a formal foresight-and-coordination architecture and its inaugural date, not continuity across governments, the quality of forecasts or whether advice changed decisions.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal placed foresight, planning, monitoring and evaluation in a centre-of-government body, then connected ministry planning units through REPLAN so cross-cutting work could be commissioned and reviewed across departmental boundaries.
preconditions: A centre-of-government mandate that can convene ministries and set common planning instruments
Planning and foresight units inside each governmental area with staff able to join joint work
Shared indicators, evaluation practice and a route from foresight outputs into budget and policy decisions
pattern.travelled: A foresight network travels when it has a convening mandate and a decision route; a named unit without ministry participation or a budget link is only an advisory label.

records.title: Agendas Mobilizadoras and green innovation alliances
records.claim: Portugal's PRR transparency portal reports 52 Agendas Mobilizadoras and Verdes representing €5,278,338,665.70 of approved investment and €3,051,632,468.10 of approved support as of 17 August 2026.

metric.name: Agendas Mobilizadoras and Verdes represented

secondMetric.name: Approved investment across the agendas

source.publisher: Portal Mais Transparência / Estrutura de Missão Recuperar Portugal, PRR project C05-i01.01

records.limits: Approved investment and support are programme commitments, not money spent, products delivered, export growth or additional private R&D. The portal aggregates consortia with different sectors and execution rates, and the figures are reported by the programme itself; they show a coordination mechanism at national scale, not that every alliance will complete its milestones by the 2026 deadline.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal used an open call to assemble firms, research organisations, clusters and public bodies into contract-based consortia, then tied public support to innovation, production, skills and technology-transfer work inside each agenda.
preconditions: A central agency able to run a competitive call and monitor many heterogeneous consortia
Firms and research organisations with enough technical and financial capacity to share a multi-year plan
Milestones, procurement and payment controls that keep public support conditional on joint delivery
pattern.travelled: Consortium programmes travel when public money buys a shared delivery obligation rather than a collection of grants; a call without a lead firm, research partner and milestone gate rarely creates durable collaboration.

records.title: Civil-court clearance and the CEPEJ monitoring series
records.claim: The CEPEJ Portugal country fiche records a 96.1% clearance rate for civil and commercial litigious cases at first instance in 2023, alongside 101.1% at second instance and 105.5% at the Supreme Court; first-instance disposition time was 267 days.

metric.name: First-instance civil and commercial clearance rate

secondMetric.name: First-instance disposition time

source.publisher: European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ), Portugal country fiche

records.limits: The clearance rate is an administrative throughput measure for one year and one case class, not a judgment-quality, access-to-justice or public-trust measure. Disposition time is a theoretical estimate derived from pending and resolved cases, and rates differ sharply by court instance; CEPEJ republishes national data and the fiche cannot identify which reforms or court-management practices caused the result.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal's courts feed case-flow data into a recurring national and European monitoring framework, making incoming, resolved and pending civil cases visible by instance and allowing backlog pressure to be compared over time.
preconditions: Court case registers with consistent definitions of incoming, resolved and pending matters
A justice statistics authority that can aggregate courts without changing the underlying case counts
A management response that uses the series to allocate judges, staff or procedural capacity
pattern.travelled: Clearance monitoring travels when case definitions stay stable and managers act on the series; a published percentage without backlog, duration and instance detail can reward fast closure rather than justice.

records.title: Lisbon–Madrid high-speed rail concession, formally abandoned
records.claim: Portugal's 2011 Council of Ministers formally abandoned the previous Lisbon–Madrid high-speed rail project, replacing its passenger priority with a freight connection through Sines, Lisbon, Setúbal, Poceirão and Madrid.

metric.name: High-speed rail projects formally abandoned

source.publisher: Diário da República, Resolução do Conselho de Ministros n.º 45/2011

records.limits: The number is categorical: one formally abandoned national project. The resolution records a policy reversal, not the project's final cost, the amount already spent or a completed line; the replacement freight priority and a later revival of high-speed planning mean this is evidence of stop-and-reframe capacity, not proof that Portugal solved rail delivery.

pattern.mechanism: Under fiscal pressure, the government stopped a politically committed passenger megaproject by resolution and redirected the corridor toward freight interoperability, changing the objective before further construction commitments accumulated.
preconditions: A cabinet with authority to revoke or redirect a concession-backed transport priority
A planning and appraisal process capable of naming the financial risk of the existing pipeline
An alternative corridor objective that can preserve part of the strategic value while dropping the original scope
pattern.travelled: Project reversals travel when governments can expose sunk costs and change scope openly; abandoning a line without a credible replacement only defers the delivery problem.

records.title: Rede Nacional de Test Beds for company experimentation
records.claim: ANI's National Innovation Report records 47 recognised Portuguese test beds and €150 million allocated to the national network for developing and testing new products and services at technology-readiness levels 5 to 9.

metric.name: Recognised test beds

secondMetric.name: PRR allocation to the test-bed network

source.publisher: Agência Nacional de Inovação, Relatório Nacional de Inovação 2024

records.limits: The count and allocation show a national experimentation infrastructure, not the number of live trials, firms served, products commercialised or regulatory changes that resulted. ANI's report says 47 were recognised at publication but gives no common utilisation definition, and the €150 million is an allocation rather than completed spending or additional private investment.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal funded and recognised shared facilities where SMEs and startups can develop and test near-market products, lowering the cost of moving an experiment from prototype toward demonstration without requiring every firm to build its own laboratory.
preconditions: Facilities with technical staff, equipment and safety procedures that can host external firms
A recognition and funding process that makes test results credible to customers and investors
A pipeline of SMEs and startups with products mature enough to test at TRL 5 to 9
pattern.travelled: Test-bed networks travel when access, measurement and procurement pathways connect a facility to real adopters; a list of subsidised facilities without utilisation data can become an infrastructure inventory rather than an experimentation capability.

records.title: Zonas Livres Tecnológicas, regulator-supervised experimentation zones
records.claim: ANI's National Innovation Report records four Portuguese Zonas Livres Tecnológicas (technological free zones) by the end of 2024, where innovators can test technology-based processes in real or near-real environments under continuous regulator supervision.

metric.name: Technological free zones identified

source.publisher: Agência Nacional de Inovação, Relatório Nacional de Inovação 2024

records.limits: Four zones are an institutional count, not a measure of trials, firms admitted, time to authorisation or successful regulatory adaptation. ANI's report uses a 31 December 2024 cutoff and does not provide a common utilisation or outcome series, so the record shows that a sandbox channel exists rather than that it is broad or effective.

pattern.mechanism: Portugal created a legal route for regulators and innovators to run controlled tests in defined physical environments, using supervised evidence from those tests to clarify or adapt rules where existing law is uncertain.
preconditions: Regulators willing to supervise experiments while protecting safety and public rights
A legal framework that permits controlled derogations or clarifications without suspending accountability
Test environments with monitoring, reporting and a route to ordinary market authorisation
pattern.travelled: Regulatory sandboxes travel when the evidence gathered in a zone can change a rule or unlock a normal licence; a protected pilot site with no route out simply postpones the regulatory decision.

records.title: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan
records.claim: India's PMGDISHA rural digital-literacy scheme enrolled 73,571,965 people, trained 63,941,718 and certified 47,836,188 by July 2024 through 20 hours of instruction in five digital-task modules.

metric.name: Candidates trained under PMGDISHA

secondMetric.name: Candidates certified under PMGDISHA

source.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India

records.limits: The government reports administrative training and third-party certification totals, not independently tested digital competence or continued use of services. The scheme covered rural areas and one person per targeted household, so it is not a population-wide adult-skills rate; the source also does not report completion quality, attrition or post-training use.

pattern.mechanism: MeitY used village-level centres, a standard five-module curriculum and external certifying agencies to move a digital-literacy offer through rural India at household scale, with certificates uploaded to DigiLocker.
preconditions: A delivery network able to reach Gram Panchayats and rural households
A common curriculum covering devices, internet, citizen services and digital payments
Independent assessment and an identity-linked certificate that makes completion portable
pattern.travelled: Digital-literacy programmes travel when training is tied to tasks people can immediately use and completion is independently checked; enrolment without post-training usage data can become a counting exercise.

records.title: SWAYAM national online-course platform
records.claim: India's SWAYAM platform offered more than 20,370 courses and recorded more than 65 million enrolments by 12 August 2026 as a national channel for flexible higher-education and skills learning.

metric.name: SWAYAM enrolments

secondMetric.name: SWAYAM courses offered

source.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India, Empowering Youth, Transforming India

records.limits: Cumulative enrolment is not a share of adults participating in learning: one person can enrol repeatedly, and the release does not provide active users, completions or the adult/student split. Course supply and enrolment show a national learning channel, not learning gains, labour-market outcomes or equal access to broadband and devices.

pattern.mechanism: The Ministry of Education assembled university courses on one open platform, letting learners study remotely and connect course participation to formal credit and certification pathways.
preconditions: Universities willing to publish reusable course material to a common technical standard
A credit and assessment framework that makes online study count beyond the platform
Connectivity and learner support good enough for participation outside campus
pattern.travelled: Open course platforms travel when enrolment can convert into recognised credit or skills; a large catalogue without completion and credential data measures supply more than continuous learning.

records.title: Unified Payments Interface, the bank-and-app network
records.claim: NPCI's UPI rail connected 731 live banks and settled 22,716.07 million transactions worth ₹28,92,138.67 crore in June 2026 through participating banks and payment apps.

metric.name: UPI transactions settled in the month

secondMetric.name: Banks live on UPI

source.publisher: National Payments Corporation of India, UPI Product Statistics

records.limits: UPI volume and bank participation show a shared transaction rail, not the quality of public-private coordination across other national objectives. NPCI publishes the figures for the system it operates, the table excludes on-us transactions from August 2018 onward, and volume says nothing about access, fraud, outages or distributional reach.

pattern.mechanism: The Reserve Bank-regulated NPCI set a common protocol and settlement layer while banks and private payment apps competed at the customer interface, allowing one public standard to scale through many firms.
preconditions: A regulated national payments operator trusted to set interoperable rules
Banks connected to a common account and settlement infrastructure
A legal and technical framework that lets private apps join without fragmenting the rail
pattern.travelled: Interoperable rails travel when the public layer is open enough for private distribution and strict enough to preserve settlement and consumer protection; transaction volume alone cannot show whether the partnership is inclusive.

records.title: CoWIN national COVID-19 vaccination platform
records.claim: India used CoWIN to register and scale COVID-19 vaccination nationally, recording more than 2.2067 billion vaccinations and 1.1093 billion registrations by 21 November 2023.

metric.name: COVID-19 vaccinations recorded by CoWIN

secondMetric.name: CoWIN registrations

source.publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India, Digital Innovations in India's Health Sector

records.limits: The counts are platform records, not unique people or a measure of protection, equity, adverse events or health outcomes. The ministry's explainer reports the totals itself and does not provide reconciliation rules, regional access gaps or the counterfactual contribution of CoWIN versus the underlying health and logistics system; the emergency programme has also ended.

pattern.mechanism: The Union government put registration, appointment, inventory-linked certification and national reporting on one platform, allowing states and vaccination sites to operate against a common record during a fast-moving shock.
preconditions: A national identity and mobile-number layer capable of handling very large registration loads
Vaccination sites and state health teams connected to a shared reporting protocol
A central operations team able to change workflows as supply and eligibility rules shifted
pattern.travelled: Crisis platforms travel when a common data model links local delivery to central visibility; registrations and doses do not by themselves establish that the system reached the hardest-to-serve groups.

records.title: Delhi Commonwealth Games, and the cost-estimate escalation
records.claim: India and Delhi hosted the Commonwealth Games in October 2010, but the Comptroller and Auditor General recorded the total estimate rising from ₹1,200 crore in the May 2003 bid to ₹18,532.31 crore by October 2010.

metric.name: Total estimated expenditure by October 2010

secondMetric.name: Initial bid estimate

source.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India, Performance Audit of XIXth Commonwealth Games

records.limits: The Games were delivered, so this is not a failed event; it documents erosion of the original cost promise. The CAG compares estimates assembled at different stages and scopes, and the October 2010 figure is not a single audited final-cost total. The audit identifies fragmented planning, late decisions and weak controls but does not attribute every rupee of the increase to one cause.

pattern.mechanism: A multi-agency event was delivered against an immovable deadline, but scope changes, late procurement and fragmented governance allowed the budget estimate to expand more than fifteen-fold between the bid and the event.
preconditions: A host agreement that bound the Union and Delhi governments to the event and its liabilities
A portfolio of venues and city works dependent on many implementing agencies
Independent audit access to plans, estimates, procurement files and delivery evidence
pattern.travelled: Large-event delivery travels badly when an immovable deadline rewards late scope acceptance; an early integrated budget and clear decision rights matter more than the event brand.

records.title: Labour Market Intelligence Programme and forward skills planning
records.claim: South Africa's Department of Higher Education and Training ran a Labour Market Intelligence Programme from 2012, published the fifth iteration of its national occupations-in-high-demand list by April 2024, and identified 138 occupations for the emerging hydrogen-economy value chain.

metric.name: National occupations-in-high-demand list iterations

secondMetric.name: Occupations identified for the hydrogen-economy value chain

source.publisher: Department of Higher Education and Training, Government of South Africa

records.limits: The programme's own ministerial account reports its outputs, and a list of occupations is a planning instrument rather than proof that enrolment, funding or curricula changed. The source describes the second phase and a third phase planned for 2025; the record therefore establishes a recurring foresight function and delivered reports, not the quality or current use of every forecast.

pattern.mechanism: DHET institutionalised a research cycle that combines labour-market data, sector studies and consultations with business, labour and government, then turns the findings into recurring occupations-in-demand lists and skills assessments for education planning.
preconditions: A department with authority to connect labour-market evidence to post-school enrolment and funding decisions
Stable research financing and partnerships with public research organisations and universities
Stakeholder channels that let employers and labour organisations challenge or refine the forecast
pattern.travelled: Foresight travels when a recurring evidence cycle changes a budget, curriculum or visa rule; publishing another list without tracing decisions that used it is only a report series.

records.title: Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme
records.claim: South Africa's IPP Office reported 95 independent power producers operational with 7,335 MW online by 31 March 2025, alongside 9,618 MW procured from 116 projects at financial close and R292.2 billion attracted for energy infrastructure.

metric.name: Operational IPP capacity

secondMetric.name: Investment attracted by projects at financial close

source.publisher: Independent Power Producers Office, South Africa, IPPPP Quarterly Report Q4 2024/25

records.limits: The IPP Office reports the programme it manages, and its figures combine several procurement windows and technologies. Operational MW and financial close show a functioning public–private delivery channel, not affordability, reliability, local ownership or emissions outcomes; terminated projects are excluded from current totals and the investment figure is attracted capital rather than completed public value.

pattern.mechanism: The state set capacity and development rules, ran repeated competitive tenders and gave private producers bankable power-purchase agreements, while Eskom and government agencies carried the grid and policy interfaces.
preconditions: A creditworthy public offtaker and a grid connection process private bidders can rely on
Transparent bid windows with standard contracts and independent evaluation
A public procurement office able to monitor construction, commercial operation and economic-development obligations
pattern.travelled: Public–private energy programmes travel when the state makes risk allocation and payment rules credible; selected capacity without financial close or operation is still only a pipeline.

records.title: MeerKAT radio telescope, a delivered national research facility
records.claim: South Africa's National Research Foundation and SARAO completed the 64-dish MeerKAT radio telescope in March 2018 on schedule and on budget, then began science operations as a precursor to the Square Kilometre Array.

metric.name: MeerKAT dishes completed

source.publisher: South African Radio Astronomy Observatory, National Research Foundation

records.limits: SARAO's institutional account states that the array was on schedule and on budget but does not publish an audited cost or baseline schedule in this record. Sixty-four dishes prove physical completion, not scientific productivity, local industrial spillovers or the performance of the larger SKA programme into which MeerKAT is being integrated.

pattern.mechanism: A national research agency led a staged telescope build, using prototype arrays, local engineering and university and industry partners to test components before integrating the full 64-dish facility in the Karoo.
preconditions: A long-lived public research institution able to hold a technically demanding project across administrations
Prototype infrastructure and specialist engineering capacity before full-scale construction
A remote site, fibre and power systems, and a scientific user community ready to operate the facility
pattern.travelled: Research infrastructure travels when prototypes, procurement and user operations are designed as one delivery chain; a completed instrument without a funded operating model becomes a monument rather than capability.

records.title: SETAs and workplace-based learning delivery
records.claim: South Africa's Sector Education and Training Authorities reported 45,146 learnership completions, 83,578 skills-programme completions and 99,778 workplace-based learning opportunities for the 2024 post-school education and training intake.

metric.name: Learnerships completed

secondMetric.name: Workplace-based learning opportunities created

source.publisher: Department of Higher Education and Training, Government of South Africa

records.limits: The ministerial statement aggregates 21 SETAs and counts opportunities and completions, not a harmonised share of adults participating in formal or non-formal learning. It does not report unique learners, demographic reach, completion quality, employment after training or the share of participants who were already in education; the figures are government-reported rather than independently audited here.

pattern.mechanism: Sector authorities levy and coordinate employer-linked training, then place learners into learnerships, skills programmes and workplace experience tied to occupational demand rather than leaving adult learning entirely to formal colleges.
preconditions: A statutory levy and sector bodies with a mandate to fund training beyond public campuses
Employers willing to host learners and assess workplace competence
Occupational standards and certification routes that make short programmes legible to workers and firms
pattern.travelled: Workplace learning travels when employers share the cost and the credential is recognised across firms; opportunity counts without learner follow-up cannot show whether skills actually accumulated.

records.title: Gauteng e-tolls, and their cancellation after public resistance
records.claim: South Africa operated Gauteng's e-toll system from December 2013 until the government withdrew the toll declaration effective 11 April 2024, ending urban e-toll charging after roughly 10.4 years.

metric.name: Years of e-toll collection before cancellation

source.publisher: Department of Transport, Government of South Africa

records.limits: The duration is calculated from the ministry's stated December 2013 start and 11 April 2024 end rather than published as a single statistic. Cancellation shows that government eventually changed a rule after resistance and a debt impasse, but it does not show how quickly the response was reached, the road programme's net value or the fiscal cost of replacing toll revenue.

pattern.mechanism: After motorists resisted the user-pay system and the funding model stalled, a joint transport, finance and provincial process replaced toll revenue with an alternative debt and maintenance arrangement and repurposed the gantries.
preconditions: A legal authority able to withdraw a toll declaration while keeping the upgraded roads in the national network
A cross-government committee able to negotiate debt, maintenance and replacement funding
Enough public pressure and political attention to reopen a scheme that had already been implemented
pattern.travelled: Responsiveness travels when institutions can change a live programme without abandoning its underlying asset; delayed reversal still leaves a long tail of debt and trust costs.

records.title: Puntos México Conectado, national digital learning centres
records.claim: Mexico's communications ministry operated Puntos México Conectado centres in all 32 states, reporting more than 410,000 enrolled members and over 260,000 course enrolments by June 2017.

metric.name: Punto México Conectado enrolled members

secondMetric.name: Course enrolments reported by the network

source.publisher: Secretaría de Infraestructura, Comunicaciones y Transportes, Government of Mexico

records.limits: The ministry reports registrations and course enrolments, not a comparable adult-skills test, completion rate or retained ability. The article is a programme announcement about a partnership and does not establish how many of the 410,000 members completed training or whether the network continued at that scale after 2017.

pattern.mechanism: The communications ministry put free digital classrooms in every state, then used equipment and curriculum partnerships with firms such as Samsung to turn connectivity points into places where people could practise new tools.
preconditions: A national network of staffed community centres rather than connectivity alone
Public funding for access and instructors across all states
Private partners willing to provide current equipment and course material
pattern.travelled: Digital-learning hubs travel when the state supplies trusted physical access and partners refresh the content; registrations without completion data should not be mistaken for population-wide proficiency.

records.title: Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro, government-workplace training
records.claim: Mexico's labour ministry linked young people to more than half a million registered workplaces for on-the-job training, reporting 2.95 million beneficiaries nationwide after five years of Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro in February 2024.

metric.name: Young people benefited

secondMetric.name: Workplaces registered to host training

source.publisher: Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social, Government of Mexico

records.limits: The ministry's total is a cumulative programme count and the workplace figure is rounded; neither shows unique completions, the quality of mentoring or whether trainees stayed employed. The government funds the stipend and insurance, so the record demonstrates a large public-private delivery interface rather than private financing of the programme.

pattern.mechanism: The labour ministry paid a stipend and social insurance while firms, shops and civil-society organisations supplied real work placements, with a shared digital platform matching young people to host workplaces.
preconditions: A public payment and insurance system able to support people outside formal employment
A large enough network of employers willing to host and report trainees
A matching and inspection platform that gives the state visibility over placements
pattern.travelled: Workplace guarantees travel when the state underwrites the first months and employers provide the learning environment; the transferable component is the matching and verification loop, not the stipend size.

records.title: COFEPRIS digital regulatory procedures
records.claim: Mexico's medicines and health-products regulator COFEPRIS completed 509,921 procedures entirely online with traceability by 5 September 2024, replacing paper hand-offs for a large share of its regulated users.

metric.name: Procedures completed fully digitally

source.publisher: Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios, Government of Mexico

records.limits: COFEPRIS publishes the number of completed digital procedures but not a before-and-after median processing time, rejection rate or compliance outcome. It is a regulator's own operational tally, and the article does not establish that every procedure type or every applicant could use the digital path.

pattern.mechanism: The regulator converted submission, tracking and completion into one traceable digital workflow, so applicants could see a case move without physically carrying documents between offices.
preconditions: A regulator with authority to make its own procedural systems mandatory
Document and identity standards that can be checked electronically
A case-management system able to expose status without exposing protected data
pattern.travelled: Digital regulatory workflows travel when traceability is designed into the case record; moving a form online without a visible status trail leaves the old bottleneck intact.

records.title: CFE Telecomunicaciones e Internet para Todos
records.claim: Mexico's state telecom operator CFE Telecomunicaciones e Internet para Todos installed 113,683 free public internet sites by September 2024, reaching 81.2 percent of its stated 140,000-site 2025 goal.

metric.name: Free public internet sites installed

secondMetric.name: Share of the 2025 site goal reached

source.publisher: CFE Telecomunicaciones e Internet para Todos, Government of Mexico

records.limits: The management report is self-reported and counts installed sites, not uptime, geographic service quality, affordability after the free offer or actual use. The 81.2 percent figure is calculated from the report's installed count and stated goal, and the programme was still short of that goal at the reference date.

pattern.mechanism: A state-owned carrier combined satellite, fibre, copper and mobile contracts with public access points, using a federal operator to reach places commercial networks had not served.
preconditions: A public operator able to aggregate several access technologies under one programme
Procurement and spectrum arrangements that reach isolated localities
Public facilities where a connection can be installed and maintained
pattern.travelled: Universal-access builds travel when a state carrier can fill commercial gaps, but the last fifth of a numerical rollout target is often the hardest and most expensive part.

records.title: Simulacro Nacional 2024, a nationwide emergency exercise
records.claim: Mexico's national civil-protection system coordinated a countrywide earthquake exercise in September 2024 in which 9,727,000 people participated, with alerts carried over 14,490 public loudspeakers and a multi-agency task force of 1.9 million personnel.

metric.name: Participants in the national drill

secondMetric.name: Public loudspeakers activated

source.publisher: Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana, Government of Mexico

records.limits: A drill records mobilisation and protocol testing, not performance in a real disaster. Participation is self-reported by agencies and organisations, and the loudspeaker count covers only listed jurisdictions; the exercise used a hypothetical earthquake and cannot establish casualty reduction or recovery speed.

pattern.mechanism: The national protection agency set one scenario, aligned federal, state and municipal responders, pushed the same alert through public infrastructure and used the exercise to expose protocol gaps before a real shock.
preconditions: A legal civil-protection system linking three government levels
An alert network and emergency command structure that can be tested at once
Schools, workplaces and households willing to participate in a common scenario
pattern.travelled: National drills travel when rehearsal is treated as an operational test rather than a ceremony; participation counts need follow-up on the failures found and fixed.

records.title: PROSPERA, and its replacement by a new scholarship authority
records.claim: Mexico abolished the 2014 decree creating PROSPERA on 31 May 2019 and ordered its people, assets and budget to transfer to the new Benito Juárez scholarship coordination within 90 days.

metric.name: Legal transition window for PROSPERA assets and staff

secondMetric.name: PROSPERA founding decree abrogated

source.publisher: Diario Oficial de la Federación, Government of Mexico

records.limits: The decree proves a formal policy and organisational change, not that the 90-day transfer happened on time or that beneficiaries experienced a seamless handover. It also does not compare PROSPERA's outcomes with the replacement scholarships, and the transition combined a programme redesign with a change in political administration.

pattern.mechanism: The executive used a new coordinating body and a single transition clause to move PROSPERA's staff, resources and education components into a different delivery model rather than preserve the old agency by inertia.
preconditions: Central budget and administrative authority over the programme's people and funds
A replacement institution ready to receive the transferred functions
A legal instrument that can abrogate the old mandate and specify a deadline
pattern.travelled: Programme replacement travels when a government can name the receiving institution and fund the handover; a deadline on paper is not evidence that service continuity survived it.

records.title: New International Airport of Mexico, and its cancellation
records.claim: Mexico cancelled the partially built Texcoco airport after construction and contracts had begun; the government's 2019 cancellation paper estimated a 100 billion peso cancellation cost, including 60 billion pesos already spent and 40 billion in non-recoverable commitments.

metric.name: Government estimate of cancellation cost

secondMetric.name: Construction expenditure already incurred at cancellation

source.publisher: Grupo Aeroportuario de la Ciudad de México, Government of Mexico

records.limits: The 100 billion peso figure is the government's own estimate and excludes or treats differently the financing and legal costs that later audits and congressional analyses debated. Cancellation is evidence of a project running backwards and of a political decision to change course, not evidence that the replacement airport delivered better value or schedule performance.

pattern.mechanism: A new administration stopped a politically contested megaproject, terminated contracts and redirected the airport strategy to a different site, accepting sunk costs in exchange for a different delivery path.
preconditions: Executive authority over the state airport holding company and the federal investment plan
A contracting and bond framework that permits negotiated termination
An alternative site and delivery institution available before the old project was abandoned
pattern.travelled: Stopping a megaproject travels as a governance option only when the government can disclose the sunk-cost trade-off and still offer a credible replacement; otherwise cancellation becomes delay with a bill attached.

records.title: e-Devlet Gateway, a shared public-service front door
records.claim: Türkiye's e-Devlet Gateway ended 2024 with 66,753,526 users, 8,309 online services and 1,080 participating institutions, including 127 private providers alongside central government, universities and municipalities.

metric.name: Registered e-Devlet Gateway users

secondMetric.name: Institutions offering services through the gateway

source.publisher: Digital Transformation Office / e-Devlet Gateway, Government of Türkiye

records.limits: User registrations and service listings measure reach and integration, not whether transactions complete, how long they take or whether private providers add value. The gateway's own statistics aggregate institutions with very different roles, and the 127 private providers are included as participants rather than evidence of joint financing or shared accountability.

pattern.mechanism: A central gateway gave public agencies, universities, municipalities and selected private providers one identity and service front door, while the state kept the common authentication and catalogue layer.
preconditions: A national identity and authentication system that many institutions can trust
A centre-of-government operator able to set integration standards
Institutions with digital case systems mature enough to expose a service end to end
pattern.travelled: Shared portals travel when the common layer is more valuable than each institution's bespoke login; a catalogue of links without transaction completion only moves the queue online.

records.title: Marmaray, the Bosphorus rail crossing
records.claim: Türkiye opened the Marmaray rail tunnel between Europe and Asia in October 2013 and the transport ministry reported 196 million passenger journeys in 2024, with 1.226 billion cumulative journeys since opening.

metric.name: Marmaray passenger journeys in 2024

secondMetric.name: Cumulative passenger journeys since opening

source.publisher: Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure, Government of Türkiye

records.limits: Passenger journeys show that the completed line is used at scale, not whether construction met its original budget or schedule. The ministry's cumulative figure is a programme-reported total, and ridership also reflects Istanbul's population, fares and the network of connecting lines rather than the tunnel alone.

pattern.mechanism: The state assembled a cross-Bosphorus rail link, integrated it with existing suburban lines and then built ridership through frequent service rather than treating the tunnel as a stand-alone monument.
preconditions: A metropolitan rail network on both sides of the crossing
Engineering and procurement capacity for a deep immersed-tube tunnel
An operating authority able to integrate timetables, fares and maintenance
pattern.travelled: A megaproject becomes capability when the operating system is funded and connected to everyday routes; a tunnel that opens without network integration will not produce this usage.

records.title: AFAD earthquake shelter and recovery operation
records.claim: After the February 2023 earthquakes, Türkiye's AFAD established 350 tent cities providing shelter for 2.5 million people, moved about 700,000 people into 414 container cities before the first winter and delivered 46,000 permanent homes within the first year.

metric.name: People sheltered in post-earthquake tent cities

secondMetric.name: Permanent disaster homes delivered within the first year

source.publisher: Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency (AFAD), Government of Türkiye

records.limits: These are government-reported outputs after a catastrophe, so they demonstrate response and recovery logistics more directly than ex ante preparedness. Shelter and home counts do not show safety, quality, displacement duration or whether the response reached every affected household; recovery was still continuing when the report was published.

pattern.mechanism: AFAD combined a national incident command system with temporary settlements, cash support and a hand-off to permanent housing, keeping shelter, health, education and debris removal in one recovery operation.
preconditions: A statutory national disaster agency with authority to coordinate ministries and provinces
Pre-existing logistics, procurement and temporary-settlement templates
Land, contractors and financing available for a second phase of permanent housing
pattern.travelled: Recovery systems travel when temporary shelter and permanent rebuilding are designed as one pipeline; a large first response can still leave a long tail if the hand-off is not funded.

records.title: MEB public lifelong-learning network
records.claim: Türkiye's Ministry of National Education reported 7,909,495 participants in public adult-learning programmes in 2024, including 6,493,700 attending in person and 1,415,795 using the HEMBA online platform; 5,305,688 earned a course certificate.

metric.name: Adult-learning participants

secondMetric.name: Participants completing courses and eligible for a certificate

source.publisher: Directorate General for Lifelong Learning, Ministry of National Education, Government of Türkiye

records.limits: The report counts course participations rather than unique adults, so repeat learners can appear more than once. Certificates indicate completion of a course, not labour-market value or durable skill acquisition, and the ministry's administrative data are not independently audited here.

pattern.mechanism: A dense network of public education centres offered locally requested courses while HEMBA moved a subset of the same provision online, allowing adult learners to enter through either a physical centre or a national platform.
preconditions: A nationwide network of public adult-education centres
A course catalogue and credential system that can be updated centrally
Digital infrastructure and instructors able to support online as well as in-person delivery
pattern.travelled: Adult-learning networks travel when local access and a common credential reinforce one another; participation totals need unique-learner and outcome data before they become a capability score.

records.title: FATİH education technology infrastructure
records.claim: Türkiye's Ministry of National Education reported that the FATİH project had installed 620,000 interactive classroom boards by 2023 and signed a five-year TÜRKSAT service contract covering about 2,000 schools.

metric.name: Interactive boards installed under FATİH

secondMetric.name: Schools covered by the continuing service contract

source.publisher: Ministry of National Education, Government of Türkiye

records.limits: Equipment counts show installation, not whether teachers use the boards or whether learning improved. The ministry reports the hardware and contract itself, and the article does not give a national uptime, maintenance-cost or student-outcome series; the 2,000-school contract is a subset of the wider rollout.

pattern.mechanism: The education ministry treated classroom hardware, connectivity and content as one procurement programme, then used a national telecom operator for continuing access rather than ending delivery at installation.
preconditions: A central school inventory and procurement authority
Electricity and connectivity in ordinary classrooms
A service provider able to maintain equipment across thousands of schools
pattern.travelled: Education technology projects travel when maintenance and teacher practice are funded alongside hardware; a board installed without a service contract quickly becomes furniture.

records.title: YEKA RES-1 renewable tender, and its cancellation
records.claim: Türkiye signed the 1,000 MWe YEKA RES-1 wind contract in February 2018 and completed its factory and R&D centre in 2019, but the Energy Ministry records that the contract was cancelled under a 2024 law.

metric.name: Wind capacity under the cancelled YEKA RES-1 contract

secondMetric.name: Factory and R&D-centre milestones completed before cancellation
