Coverage is departments and devolved administrations under standard PFI and PF2 terms only; other PPP forms such as NHS LIFT are excluded, and Scotland and Wales run their own models that the 2018 announcement did not affect. The 1992 start year is not stated in the document, whose earliest year is 1997. The figures are in a PDF: the 55-a-year and nine-a-year averages and the PF2 announcement on PDF page 5 (paragraphs 1.5 and 1.6), the 704 projects and £57 billion on PDF page 8 (paragraphs 2.2 and 2.3). The publication is HM Treasury reporting on its own programme.

pattern.mechanism: HM Treasury let departments and local bodies buy hospitals, schools, roads and prisons as long design-build-finance-operate contracts paid by performance-linked unitary charges, keeping the capital cost off the up-front budget; after value-for-money criticism it reformed the model as PF2 in 2012 and then stopped using it for new central-government projects in 2018.
preconditions: A deep domestic market of contractors, lenders and advisers able to price 25 to 30 year availability contracts.
Fiscal rules that rewarded keeping capital spending off the public balance sheet, which made the model attractive before it made it suspect.
A central unit (Partnerships UK, later the Infrastructure and Projects Authority) to standardise contracts and collect portfolio data.
pattern.travelled: The PFI model was copied widely, including by Canada and Japan; the UK case is the clearest example of an originating country closing the route for new projects while carrying the legacy portfolio for decades.

records.title: PFI Act projects and concessions
records.claim: Under the 1999 PFI Act, Japanese national and local governments had published implementation policies for a cumulative 1,219 PFI projects by 31 March 2026, 80 of them public facility operating concessions, with a cumulative initial contract value of ¥10.47 trillion (104,730 hundred-million yen).

metric.name: Cumulative PFI projects with a published implementation policy since FY1999

secondMetric.name: Cumulative PFI contract value (initial contract amounts)

source.publisher: Cabinet Office of Japan, PPP/PFI Promotion Office, PFI事業の実施状況（令和7年度）

records.limits: The count is of projects whose implementation policy was published, which the Cabinet Office tracks by its own survey; a published policy is not a delivered asset, although the note says projects cancelled during service or abandoned before service began are excluded. Most projects are small and local: the sectoral table in the same annex shows local governments sponsoring the large majority (for example 397 of 454 culture and education projects), so the record evidences a widely used procurement route rather than large national infrastructure. The contract value covers initial contract amounts where a public payment was fixed and excludes concession fees, and the annex itself says it differs from the project-scale measure in the 2026 PPP/PFI Action Plan. Nothing here shows value for money or service quality. The figures are read from charts and a table in a PDF (project counts on page 1, contract values on page 2, concessions on page 3, sector table on page 4); the summary page at https://www8.cao.go.jp/pfi/pfi_jouhou/pfi_joukyou/pfi_joukyou_r7.html states 1,219 and 80 in text. The Cabinet Office is the programme's own promoter.

pattern.mechanism: The national government legislated a standard route for private finance, design, construction and operation of public facilities, and a Cabinet Office promotion office published guidelines, case collections and annual counts, so that municipalities could procure schools, waste plants and civic buildings through PFI and, from 2011, grant operating concessions for airports and water works.
preconditions: Fiscal pressure on local governments that made spreading capital costs over a service period attractive.
Large domestic contractors and banks willing to form special-purpose companies for small and mid-size local projects.
A central promotion office able to issue standard guidance and keep the national register of projects.
pattern.travelled: Japan adapted the UK PFI model in 1999 and kept using and widening it, adding concessions in 2011, while the UK stopped using it for new central-government projects in 2018.

records.title: Dual vocational training (duale Ausbildung), and its contraction
records.claim: Germany's dual training system, in which firms employ apprentices under contracts registered by the chambers while state vocational schools teach them, recorded 475,950 new training contracts in the year to 30 September 2025, down from 569,379 in 2011, while 54,372 offered places stayed unfilled.

metric.name: New dual training contracts (BIBB survey, 1 October to 30 September)

secondMetric.name: New dual training contracts at the series peak (2009 to 2025)

source.publisher: Bundesinstitut für Berufsbildung (BIBB), Erhebung neu abgeschlossene Ausbildungsverträge zum 30.09., Tabelle 60 (Stand 05.12.2025)

records.limits: The fall of about 16 percent from the 2011 high is computed from two published values (column 1). How much of it is the collaboration weakening is contested. On the applicant side, unfilled training places rose from 17,139 in 2009 to a high of 73,431 in 2023, which points to fewer and differently choosing school leavers, demography and the shift to university. On the employer side, the same table shows the places offered (column 6) falling from 598,935 in 2011 to 530,322 in 2025, about 11 percent, including a drop of 25,338 in 2025 alone, while unfilled places fell to 54,372 and applicants left without a place or an alternative (column 3) rose to 38,784, the highest in the series; the latest year reads as firms offering fewer places, not only as missing applicants. A hostile reviewer would also say the system still enrols nearly half a million new trainees a year, the largest joint public-private training delivery in the corpus. The table does not show the share of firms that train, which is the direct measure of employer participation. The 2020 figure (467,484) is a pandemic low and 2025 sits above it. The series starts in 2009, so earlier and higher levels are not covered, and the 1969 start year (the Vocational Training Act) is not stated in the source. Figures are read from a two-page PDF table, Bundesgebiet block. BIBB is a federal institute that runs the survey with the chambers, the bodies that register the contracts.

pattern.mechanism: Federal law sets training regulations agreed with employers and unions, firms recruit and pay apprentices and deliver workplace training, chambers register contracts and run examinations, and the Länder run part-time vocational schools, so qualification is a joint product that no single party can deliver alone.
preconditions: Chambers with statutory membership able to register contracts and examine to one national standard.
Employers who treat training as recruitment and accept net training costs.
A school system that channels a large share of school leavers into apprenticeships rather than university.
pattern.travelled: The dual model is widely copied (the corpus carries Switzerland's che-dual-vet); German data show that even the reference system loses volume when the supply of school leavers and their preferences shift.

records.title: New Payments Platform, the shared fast-payment rail
records.claim: The New Payments Platform, whose payments the Reserve Bank of Australia settles one by one in central bank money through the Fast Settlement Service of its RITS system, settled a daily average of 3.6 million transactions in 2024/25, almost 19 percent more than in 2023/24, worth A$4.7 billion a day.

metric.name: Fast Settlement Service (NPP) daily average transactions settled

secondMetric.name: Fast Settlement Service (NPP) daily average value settled

source.publisher: Reserve Bank of Australia, Annual Report 2025

records.limits: The figure counts settlements in the Reserve Bank's Fast Settlement Service, which exists to settle NPP payments; it is a volume measure, not evidence of reach, outage resilience, fraud losses or how much activity is additional to existing direct entry. The annual report shows the Reserve Bank's half of the arrangement (settlement in RITS, fifteen institutions settling NPP payments directly) but does not say who built, owns or governs the NPP itself; it names NPP Australia Limited only in its glossary, so the industry side of the partnership rests on sources outside this document. The NPP is still the smaller rail for account-to-account payments: the report's Graph 2.3.4 shows bulk electronic clearing (BECS) still carrying more daily volume, and the industry's proposed decommissioning of BECS, which the report discusses, is not yet done. The 2018 launch year is not stated in the annual report. The number is on page 99 of the PDF. The rba.gov.au host refuses scripted requests (Akamai 'Access Denied'); the PDF was read through WebFetch at the same URL. The Reserve Bank reports on a service it owns and operates.

pattern.mechanism: The Reserve Bank set real-time payment objectives after its 2012 strategic review and built the Fast Settlement Service, while banks jointly financed, built and governed the switching platform and overlay services, so that every participating account could send and receive in seconds around the clock.
preconditions: A central bank willing to set outcome targets and build settlement infrastructure but leave the customer-facing rail to industry.
A concentrated banking sector able to agree a shared build and its governance.
Exchange settlement accounts for participants so each payment can settle individually in central bank money.
pattern.travelled: Fast-payment rails built by industry under central bank objectives are common; Australia's case shows the slow part is migrating legacy bulk payments, not launching the rail.

records.title: NIBSS Instant Payment (NIP)
records.claim: NIBSS Instant Payment, run since 2011 by the interbank settlement company jointly owned by the Central Bank of Nigeria and the banks, grew from 2 billion transactions in 2020 to 11 billion in 2024, with values rising from US$457 billion to US$1.1 trillion, and had 57.7 million unique users.

metric.name: NIP transactions in the year

secondMetric.name: NIP unique users (52 percent of adults)

source.publisher: AfricaNenda Foundation, The State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS 2025), NIP Nigeria case study

records.limits: The publisher is a non-profit foundation, not a statistical agency, and the case study does not name the source of its 2020 to 2024 series ('NIP data for 2020 to 2024 shows'); it is presumably NIBSS operator data, but that is an inference. The Central Bank of Nigeria's e-payment statistics page reports channels (internet, mobile app, USSD transfers) without naming NIP, and NIBSS's own pages carry press reprints that mix NIP and all e-payment totals, so no official NIP series was citable. The figures are rounded (2 and 11 billion), the 2024 value is printed as $1.1 trillion in the text and $1,171,642 million in the chart, and the dollar values are converted at unstated rates in a period of steep naira devaluation, so the value growth says little in real terms. Growth was pushed by the 2023 cash scarcity and the pandemic as much as by the rail; the same page reports 69 percent of transaction volumes from men, a large inclusion gap, and the 57.7 million users are not active-user counts. Ownership and governance (jointly owned by the CBN and banks, a board of a CBN deputy governor and bank chief executives) and the 2011 launch are stated in the same document. Figures are in a PDF, on PDF page 8 (printed page 9) and the chart that follows.

pattern.mechanism: The Bankers' Committee, the forum of the central bank and the deposit-taking banks, created a jointly owned switch in 1992 and used it to launch a 24/7 account-to-account instant payment service in 2011, with the central bank setting rules and fee caps and every bank connected, so a transfer reached any account in seconds.
preconditions: A standing forum where the central bank and banks already took joint decisions and co-owned infrastructure.
A cashless-policy push from the central bank that gave banks a reason to route retail payments electronically.
A unique bank identity layer (the Bank Verification Number) to reduce fraud on instant transfers.
pattern.travelled: NIP is one of the older African instant payment systems and a reference in AfricaNenda's regional reviews; its joint ownership model differs from rails built by a central bank alone.

records.title: InstaPay under the National Retail Payment System
records.claim: InstaPay, the real-time automated clearing house organized under the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas' National Retail Payment System framework, in which banks and e-money issuers take part, processed 4.7 billion transfers worth ₱11.6 trillion in 2025, up from 232.9 million in 2020, with 95 participating institutions in July 2026.

metric.name: InstaPay transactions in the year

secondMetric.name: InstaPay transaction value in the year

source.publisher: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, Payments Bulletin (data as of July 2026)

records.limits: Transaction counts show a heavily used rail, not who uses it: a large part of the 2025 jump (230.9 percent in volume against 57.3 percent in value) is consistent with small e-wallet cash-ins and transfers, so value per transfer fell, and the bulletin does not split person-to-person use from wallet top-ups. The participant count (87 sender-receivers and eight receive-only) is computed from the bulletin's table. The bulletin lists InstaPay among the payment systems organized under the National Retail Payment System and lists its participants by type, but does not say who operates or governs the clearing house, so the industry side of the arrangement rests on sources outside this bulletin. The 2018 start year is not stated in the bulletin, whose annual table begins in 2020. The central bank's 2024 digital payments report puts digital at 57.4 percent of retail payment volume, so cash still carries a large share. The bulletin is a slide deck PDF: the annual table is on page 6 and the participant table on page 5. bsp.gov.ph refuses scripted requests (Akamai 'Access Denied'); the PDF was read through WebFetch at the same URL. The central bank reports on a framework it regulates.

pattern.mechanism: The central bank set an interoperability framework requiring retail payment providers to join industry-run automated clearing houses, while banks and e-money issuers governed the clearing rules through a self-regulatory payment management body, so any account or wallet could pay any other in real time.
preconditions: A central bank willing to mandate interoperability but delegate rule-making to an industry body.
Mobile e-money issuers large enough to bring unbanked users onto the rail.
A national QR standard (QR Ph) to carry the rail to merchants.
pattern.travelled: The arrangement resembles Thailand's PromptPay and India's UPI in the corpus, with a stronger role for industry self-governance.

records.title: National eID ecosystem with private trust-service partners
records.claim: Estonia's state eID ecosystem, in which the state issues ID cards with certificates from a private trust-service partner and accepts the privately issued Smart-ID in its authentication service TARA, handled 27,094,512 Smart-ID authentications through TARA in 2023, 57 percent of the total, beside 22,351,282 by state ID card and Mobile-ID.

metric.name: Smart-ID authentications through the state authentication service TARA

secondMetric.name: ID card and Mobile-ID authentications through TARA

source.publisher: Riigi Infosüsteemi Amet (Estonian Information System Authority), Identiteedihalduse ja eID valge raamat 2024

records.limits: The counts are authentications through one state service, TARA, not all eID use (banks authenticate customers directly, outside TARA). The split shows a shift from state-issued means to a private credential rather than growth of joint delivery: the white paper reports that ID card and Mobile-ID signatures fell from 94.8 percent of digital signatures in 2020 to 76 percent in 2022 as Smart-ID was enabled, and state-means signatures through DigiDoc fell from 8.6 million in 2021 to 6.9 million in 2023. A hostile reviewer could read that as the state losing control of its identity layer to a private provider. The document is a strategy white paper, not a statistical release, and draws on the Police and Border Guard Board and SK ID Solutions for issuance data. The 2002 start year (first ID cards) is not stated in the source. Figures are in a PDF on PDF pages 22 and 23 (printed pages 20 and 21), text and Tables 1 to 4.

pattern.mechanism: The state made a chip ID card with authentication and signing certificates compulsory and built common authentication and signing services, while a private certification provider issued the certificates, mobile operators issued Mobile-ID SIMs and banks relied on the same credentials, so one identity layer served public and private services and later absorbed a bank-led smartphone credential.
preconditions: A compulsory national identity document with a single personal code.
A domestic trust-service provider and mobile operators willing to run certification as a business on state rules.
Banks and other large private relying parties that adopted the state credential early, giving citizens a reason to use it.
pattern.travelled: Estonia's eID model is widely cited; Smart-ID has spread to Latvia and Lithuania through the same provider, which makes the private side of the partnership the part that travelled.

records.title: Finnish Trust Network for strong electronic identification
records.claim: From May 2017 Finland's Trust Network obliged banks and mobile operators issuing strong electronic identification to let brokers resell their authentications at a regulated maximum price, cut to 3 cents in 2019, and mediated authentication events rose from an estimated 20 million in the second half of 2019 to about 60 million in the first half of 2020.

metric.name: Authentication events mediated through Trust Network brokers (estimate)

secondMetric.name: Maximum regulated wholesale price per mediated authentication (from 2019)

source.publisher: Traficom (Finnish Transport and Communications Agency) and Finnish Competition and Consumer Authority, Sähköisen tunnistamisen markkinat, Traficomin tutkimuksia ja selvityksiä 2/2021

records.limits: The volume figures are the regulators' own estimates ('arviolta') built from provider returns that some providers could not separate, and the report says it could not trace a multi-year series; for 2019 it gives only a range of 40 to 80 million. The figures are from 2020 and published in March 2021, so they are dated, and the first half of 2020 overlaps the first months of the pandemic, which also pushed public and private services online. The collaboration was regulatory compulsion as much as partnership: the report says identification providers held at least a weak monopoly over their own credentials before price caps, and the network only worked from 2019 after repeated legislative fixes, with 2020 the first full year of comprehensive brokerage. Bank credentials made up an estimated 85 to 90 percent of mediated events in late 2019, so the system depends on a few banks. The government is building a state digital identity alongside it. Figures are on PDF pages 79 and 80 (printed pages 78 and 79), section 6.5.

pattern.mechanism: Parliament and the communications regulator turned bank and mobile-operator credentials into shared national infrastructure by law: providers must sell authentications to licensed brokers at a capped wholesale price, so any public or private e-service can accept every strong credential through one contract, and the state's own Suomi.fi service buys them the same way.
preconditions: Near-universal online banking credentials already held by the population.
A regulator with the power to set and lower a wholesale price cap and enforce interconnection terms.
A state authentication service large enough to be the anchor customer for brokered identification.

records.title: Interoperable QR immediate payments, built by the banks and the Banco Central de Bolivia
records.claim: Bolivia's banks first offered QR payments under their own SIMPLE standard, and the Banco Central de Bolivia then made QR transfers interoperable across banks, cooperatives, housing lenders and development finance institutions with a universal standard compatible with the banks' codes, mandatory electronic channels and free transfers; immediate QR payments rose from 6 million operations in 2021 to 892 million in 2025, 86 percent of electronic fund transfer orders that year.

metric.name: Immediate payments by QR code processed in the year

secondMetric.name: Value of immediate payments by QR code in the year

source.publisher: Banco Central de Bolivia, Informe de Vigilancia del Sistema de Pagos 2025

records.limits: Both numbers are data labels on Gráfico 17 of a 72-page PDF (PDF page 35, printed page 29), with the 86 percent share on Gráfico 18 on the next page; there is no machine-readable series. The central bank is the regulator, the standard-setter and the reporter, so this is the system's owner grading its own system. The collaboration mixes a private standard with a public mandate: the banking system built SIMPLE, the BCB built a compatible universal standard and imposed interoperability and free transfers, and private institutions and the clearing houses ACCL and UNILINK carried it out. The 2025 jump coincided with Bolivia's dollar shortage, fuel queues and rising inflation, which push people off cash; the value series is in nominal bolivianos and overstates real growth in a year of high inflation. A payment count does not show inclusion: the report gives no figure for first-time account holders. The series counts every immediate QR payment processed through the clearing houses and the BCB's settlement module, not only codes generated under QR BCB Bolivia: the banks' own SIMPLE QR standard came first, the BCB's 2021 vigilance report describes the BCB's compatible QR standard in its settlement module as due in the last quarter of 2022, and the BCB's QR page (https://www.bcb.gob.bo/?q=pagos_qr_bcb_bolivia) calls QR BCB 'un solo estándar universal compatible con todos los QR implementados por el sistema financiero'. The 2021 figure therefore predates the BCB standard, and the start year is the first year of the series, not the launch of either standard.

pattern.mechanism: The banking system launched its own QR standard, and the Banco Central de Bolivia then built a universal QR standard compatible with it into its settlement module, required every financial institution to offer electronic channels and free transfers, and settled QR payments through its module and the private clearing houses, so each institution's app could pay any account in the system.
preconditions: Prior interconnection of more than 90 percent of financial institutions for electronic transfers, which the BCB had already mandated
A central bank with regulatory power over every deposit-taking institution, including cooperatives and development lenders
Mobile banking apps already offered by most institutions, so the QR standard only had to be added
pattern.travelled: The same move as Thailand's PromptPay and Malaysia's DuitNow, made by a central bank in a lower-income, cash-heavy economy and accelerated by a currency shortage rather than by a planned cash-reduction policy.

records.title: Plan Nacional de Viviendas Familia Feliz, and its intake freeze
records.claim: By May 2024 the Dominican government's Familia Feliz plan, in which private developers build low-cost homes and the state pays down-payment, tax and mortgage-rate subsidies, had built 3,979 homes and assigned RD$1,108 million in subsidies.

metric.name: Homes built under the plan since launch

secondMetric.name: Subsidies assigned (Bono Inicial, Bono Itbis and Bono Tasa 7 Años)

source.publisher: Ministerio de la Presidencia de la República Dominicana, press note of 13 May 2024

records.limits: The numbers come from a ministry press note quoting the minister, not from a statistical series, and the government is reporting on its own flagship. 'Built' is not 'handed over': the same note says 704 apartments were delivered in January to May 2024 and 934 were waiting to be inaugurated. It also promised 9,600 deliveries in 2024, and no official page opened today gives a cumulative delivered total to check that against; Diario Libre (12 May 2026) reports the housing ministry putting Familia Feliz deliveries at 5,922 units since 2020, which, if right, means the 2024 promise was badly missed. That figure is press only and is not used. The programme's intake has stopped: FONVIVIENDA's news item of 26 April 2026 (https://fonvivienda.gob.do/2026/04/26/ministro-ito-bisono-reafirma-continuidad-del-programa-familia-feliz-entrega-144-apartamentos-en-laderas-del-este-vf/) says projects approved up to 30 December 2025 continue unchanged, that applications made up to that date are being re-evaluated, and that the focus is on finishing and handing over projects approved up to 2025, and it names no intake after that date; the status is eroded for that reason, although deliveries from the pipeline continue (890 apartments across Familia Feliz and Mi Vivienda in the first half of 2026, per FONVIVIENDA, not split by programme). A few thousand homes is small against the national housing deficit. The private side is paid by subsidy and mortgage, so this is a subsidy-for-supply model; banks still screen buyers through pre-approval, which excludes the informal poor. The start year is taken from Decreto 191-21, which created the FONVIVIENDA trust.

pattern.mechanism: The Presidency, and since Decreto 114-25 the housing ministry, ran a national trust that certifies private housing projects and pays each buyer's down payment, sales tax and seven years of mortgage-rate relief, so private developers and banks build and finance low-cost homes that the state does not build itself.
preconditions: Law 189-11 on mortgage development and trusts, which lets each project sit in a certified autonomous trust that protects buyers
A banking sector willing to lend long-term mortgages to lower-income buyers once the state covers the down payment and part of the rate
Domestic developers able to build several thousand units across provinces
pattern.travelled: A version of Mexico's and Brazil's developer-led subsidised housing models (Minha Casa Minha Vida), run at much smaller scale and paused after a change of ministry.

records.title: Bank of Israel COVID-19 small-business credit programme
records.claim: After the Monetary Committee decided on 6 April 2020 to lend banks three-year fixed-rate money for credit to small and micro businesses, the Bank of Israel had NIS 1.2 billion outstanding under the programme by 30 April 2020 and NIS 28.1 billion by 31 March 2021.

metric.name: Long-term loans to the banking system for credit to small businesses, balance outstanding

secondMetric.name: Same programme, balance outstanding 24 days after the decision

source.publisher: Bank of Israel, monthly report on programmes operated in the financial markets in view of the coronavirus crisis (press release, 7 April 2021)

records.limits: The site answers scripted requests with a Radware bot-verification page; the table was read in a normal browser at the same URL, so a reviewer needs a browser to check it. The figures are the Bank reporting on its own programme. They are balances of central-bank loans to banks, not credit that reached firms and not a count of businesses: how much of the money became new small-business lending, rather than refinancing, is not shown. The programme was not continuous: the footnote says it ran first until the end of May 2020 and was renewed in August, and the balance sits at NIS 4.6 billion from May to July. Part of the March 2021 balance comes from a second pillar of four-year loans at minus 0.1 percent decided on 22 October 2020. The cited page's last row is 31 March 2021; the status rests on a later report in the same series (7 July 2021, boi.org.il/en/communication-and-publications/press-releases/monthly-report-on-programs-the-bank-of-israel-is-operating-in-the-financial-markets-in-view-of-the-coronavirus-crisis-12/), which records a Monetary Committee decision of 5 July 2021 to end the programme on 1 October 2021 or once NIS 40 billion had been extended, and a balance of NIS 37.2 billion on 30 June 2021. The same table shows the Bank's other rapid moves (repo from 15 March, dollar-shekel swaps from 18 March, government bond purchases from 23 March 2020, NIS 8.5 billion outstanding by 31 March), which are monetary operations rather than programme changes and are not the claim. The State Comptroller's 2021 COVID-19 special report found that financial regulators prepared rapidly but that timeframes for handling loan requests were not set, which concerns the separate state-guaranteed loan funds.

pattern.mechanism: The Monetary Committee created a dedicated funding line for banks, conditioned on lending to small and micro businesses, within weeks of the first lockdown, and reopened and extended it with cheaper terms as the crisis continued.
preconditions: A central bank with legal room to lend to banks against a lending purpose
A concentrated banking system that can pass a funding line to small firms quickly
Policy rates near zero, so the subsidy had to come through term and price of funding
pattern.travelled: Funding-for-lending schemes of this shape ran in the United Kingdom from 2012 and at the European Central Bank as targeted longer-term refinancing operations; Israel's version was set up and drawn within one month.

records.title: Policy Horizons Canada, the federal foresight unit, and its 2024 disruption scan
records.claim: Policy Horizons Canada, which describes itself as the Government of Canada's centre of excellence in foresight and reports through the Deputy Minister of Employment and Social Development Canada, published Disruptions on the Horizon 2024, which identified and assessed 35 possible disruptions using survey input from around 500 stakeholders, colleagues and foresight experts across the Government of Canada and beyond.

metric.name: Stakeholders, colleagues and foresight experts whose survey input assessed the disruptions (approximate, as stated)

secondMetric.name: Possible disruptions identified and assessed in the report

source.publisher: Policy Horizons Canada, Government of Canada, Disruptions on the Horizon 2024 (PH4-198/2024E-PDF)

records.limits: The unit is reporting on its own work, and the 500 is stated as 'around 500', an approximate count of survey inputs rather than a measure of whether any department used the scan; the report itself says its content does not necessarily represent the views of the Government of Canada. The description as centre of excellence is in the report's disclaimer; the reporting line through the Deputy Minister of Employment and Social Development Canada is stated on the unit's about page (https://horizons.service.canada.ca/en/about-us/index.shtml), not in the report. Both figures appear on the web version at the source URL and in the PDF edition (pages 5 and 7 of https://horizons.service.canada.ca/en/2024/disruptions/Disruptions_on_the_Horizon_2024_report.pdf). No published budget, staff count or uptake figure was found: Employment and Social Development Canada's 2024-25 Departmental Results Report does not mention the unit, so the record evidences a standing federal function producing a dated whole-of-government scan with a deputy minister steering committee named in its acknowledgements, not the influence of that scan on policy. Whether the Disruptions report is annual was not verified: no 2023 or 2025 edition was found at the corresponding addresses. Started is 1996, when secondary histories place the unit's predecessor, the Policy Research Secretariat, in the Privy Council Office, renamed Policy Research Initiative in 2000 and Policy Horizons Canada around 2011 to 2012; that lineage was not verified on an official page today and the foresight mandate as now worded dates from the later renaming. The unit sits inside a line department rather than at the centre of government, which limits its reach.

pattern.mechanism: A small dedicated foresight unit inside the federal public service, governed by a deputy minister steering committee, runs recurring horizon scans and surveys hundreds of officials and outside experts to rate disruptions by likelihood, impact and timing, and trains and networks foresight practitioners across departments.
preconditions: A permanent home and budget line inside the public service that survives changes of government
Senior sponsorship at deputy minister level so departments answer the survey and read the result
A network of departmental foresight practitioners to carry the work into policy files
pattern.travelled: Policy Horizons' published foresight training manual is listed as a toolkit by the OECD Observatory of Public Sector Innovation; this was seen in search results only and not verified at source.

records.title: Framtidskommissionen, the Prime Minister's time-limited future commission
records.claim: The Swedish government appointed Framtidskommissionen, chaired by Prime Minister Fredrik Reinfeldt, in November 2011 to identify the societal challenges Sweden faces in the longer term, and by its final report in March 2013 it had held eight meetings, organised 40 open meetings, seminars and workshops, published twelve background reports and an anthology, and carried out four sub-inquiries.

metric.name: Background reports (underlagsrapporter) published by the commission

secondMetric.name: Open meetings, seminars and workshops organised by the commission

source.publisher: Government Offices of Sweden (Regeringskansliet), Ds 2013:19 Svenska framtidsutmaningar, final report of Framtidskommissionen

records.limits: The commission reports on itself, and the figures count activities, not influence on policy; the foreword says identifying challenges, not proposing how to meet them, was its purpose. The figures are in a 316-page PDF, on PDF page 17 (printed page 14) and repeated on PDF page 310 (printed page 291), where the November 2011 appointment and the membership are also stated. It was a time-limited commission of ministers from one coalition and outside members, and it ended with the report: it evidences the existence and mandate of a centre-of-government foresight exercise and, for the construct's third element, its lack of continuity. The next government ran its own time-limited project, Mission: The Future, from February 2015 to April 2016, with a Minister for Strategic Development from 3 October 2014 to 25 May 2016 (government.se, https://www.government.se/government-of-sweden/prime-ministers-office/mission-the-future/, read in a browser because the site returns 403 to scripts), and Sweden's innovation agency Vinnova wrote in 2024 that in strategic institutionalisation of foresight for policy Sweden is 'a weak case' (Strategic Foresight for Innovation, PDF page 32). Status is concluded rather than dismantled because both vehicles were set up as time-limited and no source read today shows either was cut short.

pattern.mechanism: The head of government chairs a time-limited commission of ministers, social partners and researchers that commissions background reports and runs public meetings across the country to name long-term challenges, then publishes one report and disbands.
preconditions: A head of government willing to chair it personally
A secretariat inside the Government Offices for the life of the commission
A successor structure to carry the work on, which was missing here
pattern.travelled: The format recurred under the following government as Mission: The Future (2015 to 2016), which was also time-limited.

records.title: Matching Fund Kedaireka university-industry matching grants
records.claim: Indonesia's Directorate General of Higher Education, Research and Technology funded 427 university-industry collaboration proposals through the Kedaireka Matching Fund in 2021, its first year, and 1,093 in 2022.

metric.name: Matching Fund proposals funded

secondMetric.name: Matching Fund proposals funded in the first year

source.publisher: Directorate General of Higher Education, Research and Technology (Ditjen Diktiristek), news release 'Matching Fund-Kedaireka Akselerasi Riset dan Inovasi Perguruan Tinggi', 13 August 2023, as archived by the Internet Archive on 29 April 2025

records.limits: The source is the ministry's own news release, and the cited URL is an Internet Archive copy: the original host (dikti.kemdikbud.go.id) no longer answers, and the successor ministry's copy on kemdiktisaintek.go.id sits behind a Cloudflare human-verification check that this protocol does not get past. The release is self-reporting, not an annual report or audit. The counts are funded proposals, not distinct firms or universities, and the release gives no count of partner firms. Partners can be businesses, industry or government bodies ('pihak bisnis, industri, maupun pemerintahan'), so not every funded proposal is a university-firm pairing. The figures show money granted, not research or commercial results. A separate ministry release of 15 September 2022 (same archive) says 5,407 proposals were submitted in 2022 against 1,231 in 2021, so roughly one in five 2022 proposals was funded; it also reports Rp 11.2 trillion of combined ministry and partner 'collaboration funds' for 2022, which mixes partner and possibly in-kind contributions and is not used here. No funded counts for 2023 to 2025 were found at an open official source. The programme was renamed Dana Padanan for 2024 and passed to the new Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Technology after the October 2024 restructuring; the programme site (backoffice.kedaireka.id) lists a 2025 call and a July 2025 award announcement, which is the basis for 'operating', but not the scale of those rounds, and the 2025 budget cuts to the ministry may have reduced it.

pattern.mechanism: The higher-education directorate built an online matchmaking platform (Kedaireka) where university staff and firms register a partnership, then paid public money to match what the partner commits, so the state funds only collaborations a partner has already put resources into.
preconditions: A national register of lecturers and higher-education institutions to verify applicants
A ministry budget line for competitive grants that can be paid to universities within the fiscal year
Firms willing to commit cash or in-kind resources before public money is released
pattern.travelled: Matching grants for university-industry projects are common (Uruguay's ANII Alianzas para la Innovación, ury-anii-alianzas, is one in the corpus); Kedaireka's variation is the platform that requires the partnership to be registered before a proposal can be filed, which let it scale to over a thousand funded projects in its second year.

records.title: Plan Nacional de Relocalizaciones, moving households out of flood-prone land
records.claim: Uruguay's national housing directorate relocated 2,618 households from flood-prone or contaminated land between 2015 and 2020 under the Plan Nacional de Relocalizaciones and related agreements with departmental governments, against a target of 3,500 to 6,000 households by 2025.

metric.name: Households relocated (cumulative)

secondMetric.name: Households relocated (cumulative, previous reported value)

source.publisher: Ministerio de Ambiente, NDC monitoring technical sheet No. 61 'Relocalizaciones' (March 2021, version 1.1), indicator compiled by the Dirección Nacional de Vivienda (DINAVI, MVOT) from administrative records

records.limits: The number is in a six-page PDF: page 1 gives 'Último valor disponible 2.618 (2020)' and page 4 the version history (2,245 for 2019, 2,618 for 2020); pages 5 and 6 give the yearly totals 294, 442, 660, 438, 411 and 373 for 2015 to 2020, which sum to 2,618. The headline on page 1 ('A 2025 se han relocalizado al menos entre 3.500 y 6.000 hogares') is the 2025 target written as if achieved, and the sheet's own data show 2,618 by 2020, below the low end of that target; no later official value was found, so whether the target was met is not shown. The count mixes flood-prone and contaminated land and does not split them, and it includes relocations after specific floods ('Inundados 2015', 'Inundados 2017'), which are recovery rather than preparation. It counts households, not people, and says nothing about whether vacated land stayed empty, which the sheet itself names as a condition that depends on departmental enforcement. The plan predates 2015, but the sheet's series starts with the 2015 to 2019 housing plan, so 'started' is the first year counted, not the plan's creation. The sheet states the plan's objective as reversing social segregation and territorial fragmentation, so it is a settlement and housing policy as much as a risk-reduction one; it is filed here because the same sheet classes it as a climate-adaptation measure. Status 'operating' rests on the sheet naming the 2020 to 2024 five-year housing plan as the plan's current frame; no count after 2020 was found. The sheet is a government monitoring document for Uruguay's climate pledge, self-reported by the ministry that runs the programme.

pattern.mechanism: The national housing directorate co-finances departmental relocation projects that move households from land that floods repeatedly into new or purchased homes, with multidisciplinary teams handling each move and the department responsible for keeping the vacated land unoccupied.
preconditions: Flood-risk maps and settlement censuses precise enough to identify which households to move
Departmental governments that co-execute and police the vacated land
A national housing budget able to buy or build replacement homes year after year
pattern.travelled: Relocation out of flood plains is the slow, preventive counterpart to evacuation; it is listed in Uruguay's climate-adaptation pledge, which is how it came to be measured.

records.title: Floating the birr, July 2024
records.claim: The National Bank of Ethiopia floated the birr on 29 July 2024, and by 20 September the former official rate had moved from 57.8 to an indicative 119.2 birr per US dollar while the parallel-market spread over it fell from 96 percent to around 5 percent.

metric.name: Parallel-market spread over the NBE indicative rate (around)

secondMetric.name: Parallel-market spread over the official rate before the float

source.publisher: International Monetary Fund, Country Report No. 24/318, Ethiopia: First Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement, staff report

records.limits: The numbers are in paragraph 6 of the staff report ('moving from 57.8 birr per US dollar on July 26 to an indicative rate of 119.2 on September 20 ... The parallel market spread to the indicative rate collapsed from 96 percent to around 5 percent over the same period'); the eLibrary HTML has no page numbers. The 5 is approximate as published. What responded fast was the rule change once decided, not the decision: the report estimates the overvaluation at 52 percent in 2022/23, so the distortion was years old, and the float was a prior action for the IMF arrangement approved on 29 July 2024, while Ethiopia was seeking a debt restructuring, with calls to Eurobond holders held from December 2023. Responsiveness here is a government acting under financing pressure and external conditionality, not on its own timetable. The same paragraph says FX liquidity stayed limited and the interbank market inactive, and the second review (Country Report 25/027) records the premium widening to a peak of 16 percent on 22 October 2024 before falling back to single digits. The IMF is a party to the programme and its staff assessment is not an independent evaluation; the costs of the depreciation (inflation pass-through, the burden on importers and households) are not shown by this number.

pattern.mechanism: The central bank replaced an administered exchange rate with a market-determined one in a single directive, moved FX surrender from itself to commercial banks and lifted import bans and controls at the same time, while tight monetary policy held the new rate near the old parallel rate.
preconditions: External financing (here the IMF arrangement) large enough to absorb the transition
A central bank able to tighten liquidity enough to stop the float turning into a spiral
Commercial banks able to quote and report FX rates daily
pattern.travelled: Egypt (2016) and Nigeria (2023 to 2024) unified rates under similar pressure; Cuba's 2021 unification (cub-ordenamiento) fragmented again, which is what the widening to 16 percent in October 2024 warned of here.

records.title: COVID-19 vaccination campaign
records.claim: Bolivia's health authorities reported to WHO that 7,505,389 people, 64 per 100 population, had received at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose by 29 December 2023, from a first dose given on 30 January 2021, with 6,307,628 (54 per 100) completing the primary series.

metric.name: People vaccinated with at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose

secondMetric.name: People who completed the primary series (last dose)

source.publisher: World Health Organization, COVID-19 dashboard vaccination data (vaccination-data.csv)

records.limits: The figures are Bolivia's own reports to WHO (DATA_SOURCE 'REPORTING'), with no independent coverage survey behind them. Nearly half the population never completed the primary series (54 per 100), first-dose reach was 64 per 100, and boosters reached 2,521,192 people, 22 per 100, so the record shows a partial delivery, well below the near-universal reach of the strongest campaigns; it is filed because the campaign did reach a majority nationally, on the same terms as ven-covid-vaccination (50 per 100 completed). The VACCINES_USED field is empty, so the record cannot show which products were used or where the doses came from, and evidences distribution only. The per-100 rates divide by WHO's population estimate. Vaccination is a response to one shock, not proof of general preparedness, and the file was last updated in December 2023. The source is a CSV with no prose; the numbers are read from one row. The WHO dashboard address covid19.who.int/who-data/vaccination-data.csv now returns an HTML page, so the cited URL is the blob the dashboard serves, the same one ven-covid-vaccination cites.

pattern.mechanism: Bolivia's health ministry ran a national COVID-19 campaign through its routine immunisation network and mass vaccination points, and reached a majority of the population with a first dose within three years.
preconditions: A routine immunisation programme with a cold chain reaching rural municipalities
A supply of doses large enough for a national campaign, however obtained
Registers good enough to count who received a second dose
pattern.travelled: Cuba (cub-covid-vaccination) reached far higher completion on domestic vaccines and Venezuela (ven-covid-vaccination) a similar partial reach; the Bolivian case sits between them, with a smaller gap between first dose and completion than Venezuela's.

records.title: County and city general secondary schools for adults (licea ogólnokształcące dla dorosłych)
records.claim: Poland's county governments and cities with county rights ran general secondary schools for adults whose enrolment rose from 26,443 pupils in 2010 to 47,584 in 2013, fell to 16,470 in 2021 and recovered to 26,734 in 2024, according to Statistics Poland's Local Data Bank.

metric.name: Pupils in general secondary schools for adults governed by country powiats and by cities with powiat rights (sum of BDL variables 473647 and 8836)

secondMetric.name: Same sum at its 2013 high, the largest value since the country-powiat series begins in 2010

source.publisher: Statistics Poland (GUS), Local Data Bank (BDL), subject P2031 'General secondary schools for adults', variables 473647 (pupils, governed by powiat self-government, country powiats) and 8836 (pupils, governed by cities with powiat rights), Poland

records.limits: The figures are computed: GUS publishes the two governing-body series separately (2024: 13,857 in country powiats and 12,877 in cities with powiat rights; 2013: 30,667 and 16,917; 2010: 11,917 and 14,526; 2021: 8,046 and 8,424) and this record adds them. The country-powiat series starts in 2010, so the sum cannot be taken further back, and the city series alone shows a break (40,439 in 2000, 5,259 in 2006, 18,038 in 2007) that tracks the restructuring of secondary schooling and a change in classification, not a real swing. These schools are a minority of adult general secondary schooling: in 2024 the same subject counts 102,881 pupils in total, of whom county and city governments hold about 26 percent, gminas, voivodships and central administration another 1,360, social organisations and associations 5,277, and the remaining roughly 69,500 sit in schools run by other bodies, which the variables read here do not break out. The 2013 high was a two-year surge from 23,737 in 2011 that the source does not explain, and the 2024 count is back at its 2010 level after three years of growth, so the record is filed as operating: the fall from 2013 to 2021 reads as a surge unwinding rather than a lost capability, and a reader who treats 2013 as the baseline would call it eroded. BDL labels the school year by its start year; the API response does not say so, so '2024' most likely means 2024/25. A pupil count is enrolment, not completion or a matura pass, and it covers general secondary schooling only: adult vocational schools, post-secondary schools, courses and employer training are outside it. The 1999 start is the year Poland's county tier was created and given secondary schools; it was not read at the cited source.

pattern.mechanism: Counties and cities with county rights, which own Poland's public secondary schools, keep evening and extramural general secondary classes open for adults who want the same matura a teenager earns, tuition-free and funded through the public education budget.
preconditions: A county tier of local government that owns secondary schools and decides which adult classes to open
A national exam and certificate system that treats an adult's matura the same as a teenager's
A per-pupil public education budget that follows adult pupils into local-government schools

records.title: Kolej Komuniti part-time and lifelong-learning (Pembelajaran Sepanjang Hayat) courses
records.claim: Malaysia's public community colleges, run by the Ministry of Higher Education, counted 259,788 part-time students, including participants in Pembelajaran Sepanjang Hayat lifelong-learning courses, in 2024, against 259,810 in 2023, according to the ministry's Statistik Pendidikan Tinggi 2024.

metric.name: Part-time students in community colleges, total, part-time including PSH programme (Table 5.4)

secondMetric.name: Same count for the previous year, same table

source.publisher: Ministry of Higher Education Malaysia (Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi), Statistik Pendidikan Tinggi 2024, chapter 5 (Kolej Komuniti), Table 5.4 'Number of Part Time Students based on State of Institution and Gender by Community Colleges 2023-2024', source TVET Coordination Division, Department of Polytechnic and Community College Education

records.limits: The ministry reports on its own colleges. The number sits in a PDF: Table 5.4 runs over several pages and the national total is on page 42 of the 72-page chapter file (printed page 143), with the note 'Part Time Student includes PSH programme'. The table does not split PSH short-course participants from part-time certificate and diploma students, does not give ages, and counts enrolments rather than unique people, so one adult taking three short courses can count three times and many PSH courses last hours or days. Against roughly 23 million Malaysians of working age it is about one participation per hundred adults, which is a reach figure, not a participation rate comparable with Eurostat or PIAAC. Earlier editions of the same publication give 238,581 (2018), 222,675 (2019), 118,455 (2020), 140,501 (2021) and 245,909 (2022), so the count halved in the pandemic and has since passed its pre-pandemic level; those figures are in the 2019, 2021 and 2023 chapter files, not at the cited URL. The 2025 edition of chapter 5 no longer carries a part-time table, so 2024 is the latest year published and the status rests on that year. The 2001 start is the year the community college system began operating as commonly reported; it was not read at the cited source.

pattern.mechanism: The higher education ministry uses its national network of community colleges, built for post-secondary vocational certificates, to also run short and part-time courses for local adults, and counts them in its annual statistics.
preconditions: A network of public colleges spread across districts, close to where adults live
Short-course funding inside the college budget so courses can be cheap or free
A ministry statistics unit that collects part-time enrolment college by college

records.title: North-South eastern expressway BOT sections, and the retreat to public investment
records.claim: Vietnam built three component projects of the 2017-2020 North-South eastern expressway phase, 178 km at about VND 25,343 billion, as BOT public-private partnerships, then financed all ten 2021-2025 component projects on the Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City stretch as public investment, and in June 2025 the Ministry of Construction reported that it had asked the Prime Minister to keep widening the corridor with public investment money, leaving PPP as a later option once tolls were collected.

metric.name: 2021-2025 phase component projects on the Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City stretch procured as PPP

secondMetric.name: 2017-2020 phase component projects built as BOT, the peak
secondMetric.unit: component projects (178 km, about VND 25,343 billion)

source.publisher: Government of Viet Nam portal (baochinhphu.vn), report of the Ministry of Construction's study on widening the North-South eastern expressway, 25 June 2025

records.limits: The figures are the Ministry of Construction's own account, relayed by the Government's e-newspaper; no audit body has published them. The zero is read off the page, not printed as a number: the ministry lists 11 public-investment component projects, 10 of them from the 2021-2025 phase, against 3 BOT projects from 2017-2020. The full 2021-2025 phase was 12 component projects of about 729 km at VND 146,990 billion, all assigned to public investment by National Assembly Resolution 44/2022/QH15 (scanned PDF at datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2022/01/44-qh.signed.pdf: 729 km in 12 component projects as public investment on page 1, Article 2.2; VND 146,990 billion on page 2, Article 2.5). The peak was itself a retreat from a plan. The Ministry of Transport listed eight sections for PPP in December 2017 (Decision 3535/QD-BGTVT, baochinhphu.vn, 26 December 2017), and only three reached contract, out of 11 component projects over 654 km. Most of the money in those three came from the state. The Government portal of 28 April 2024 puts Cam Lam-Vinh Hao at VND 8,925 billion with about 5,139 billion of state capital, and Dien Chau-Bai Vot at 11,157 billion with about 6,067 billion. The same page records the opening of Cam Lam-Vinh Hao and of Dien Chau-Bai Vot as far as National Highway 46B, with Nha Trang-Cam Lam already in service; the Ministry of Transport announced the full Dien Chau-Bai Vot opening for 30 June 2024 (baochinhphu.vn, 28 June 2024). Construction started in 2020-2021, per the Ministry of Transport on the 2024 page. The retreat is a choice as much as a market failure: the same 2025 page says the ministry's own study found BOT widening highly feasible, and it chose public investment, citing toll levels and the push to disburse public funds. This is one corridor. The record does not show whether PPP procurement fell on other expressways. The question is still open: a pre-feasibility report of June 2026 (baochinhphu.vn, 6 June 2026) proposes public investment for 15 component projects and PPP with state support only for the three existing BOT sections. That is a proposal, not a decision.

pattern.mechanism: The transport ministry split the corridor into component projects and offered some of them to BOT investors, with state capital covering more than half of each project's cost and tolls repaying the private share. For the next phase the National Assembly financed every section from the budget, with the state to recover its outlay through tolls, which took private investors out of the corridor.
preconditions: A ministry able to package a long corridor into sections a domestic investor can finance
State capital support large enough to make toll revenue cover the private share
A budget and a legislature willing to finance the corridor directly when investors do not close, which is also what ended the partnership route
pattern.travelled: Viability-gap BOT on a national trunk road shows how far a state will go before it simply pays for the road itself: here, once public money was available and the schedule was political, the partnership share went to zero.

records.title: Neelum-Jhelum Hydropower Project, and its shutdown
records.claim: WAPDA's subsidiary NJHPC's 969 MW Neelum-Jhelum project, under construction from January 2008 and substantially completed in 2018, had cost Rs 423,446 million by June 2023 against Rs 84,502 million in the 2002 revised PC-I, nine years late; it peaked at 4,940.67 GWh in 2020 and was forced into complete shutdown by a head race tunnel failure on 2 April 2024 (the auditor counts 1,797.704 million units lost in FY2023-24), after an earlier tail race tunnel collapse in July 2022.

metric.name: Cost overrun against the 1st revised PC-I (2002), actual expenditure to June 2023

secondMetric.name: Peak annual generation, before the 2022 and 2024 tunnel collapses

source.publisher: Auditor-General of Pakistan, Performance Audit Report on Neelum Jhelum Hydropower Project, audit year 2022-23

records.limits: This is a delivery that ran backwards twice: badly over cost and schedule while it was being built, then lost its output after it was finished. The overrun is measured against the 2002 revision, which is the auditor's choice of baseline; against the 1989 original (Rs 15,012 million) it would be far larger, and against the 2018 fourth revision (Rs 506,808 million) the project came in under. Part of the rupee overrun is exchange-rate depreciation and interest during construction, which a cost-performance reading should not charge entirely to delivery. The plant never reached its design output of 5,150 GWh even at its 2020 peak, partly because India's upstream Kishanganga project and a higher environmental flow reduced water, which management cites and the auditor rejects. The overrun percentage (about 400 percent) is our computation from two published figures, and the Rs 338,944 million is the auditor's own subtraction. The 2024 shutdown is documented in a second AGP report; the expected restart date circulating in the press is not from this source and is not claimed here. Management disputes several findings and never convened the Departmental Accounts Committee, so the report records the auditor's view without a settled reply.

pattern.mechanism: WAPDA started tunnelling in difficult Himalayan geology before design issues were settled, and the planning ministry re-approved the cost four times rather than stopping or re-scoping the project, so the bill rose with each revision and the tunnels later failed where weak rock had been flagged.
preconditions: A state utility able to borrow and add a consumer surcharge to keep financing a project as costs rose
A project appraisal system that approves revised PC-Is after the fact instead of gating on final design
A strategic water-rights deadline with India that pushed construction to start before geology and design were resolved

records.title: Tarbela Fourth Extension Hydropower Project
records.claim: WAPDA built a 1,410 MW powerhouse on Tarbela Dam's fourth tunnel, effective April 2012 and commissioned in 2018; the World Bank recorded it as completed on time and below its estimated cost, with a capital cost expected at US$749 million.

metric.name: Expected capital cost of T4HP, physical works and supervision excluding interest during construction

secondMetric.name: Electricity generated since commissioning

source.publisher: World Bank, Tarbela Fourth Extension Hydropower Project (P115893) restructuring paper RES40334

records.limits: The lender is grading its own project: 'on time and in less than estimated cost' is the World Bank's sentence in a restructuring paper, not an audit, and the paper gives no baseline figure, so the size of the saving cannot be checked from this source. The cost is an expectation in 2019, before every work was closed; the intakes for tunnels 3 and 4 were still being finished, and the loan closing date moved from 2018 to 2024 because the same project was extended to build T5HP. That fifth extension, financed under the same project number, is rated Moderately Satisfactory in the 2023 ISR and was due for completion in 2025; T4's record is not the record of the whole project. The World Bank financed about 90 percent of the civil and electro-mechanical works, so the case shows WAPDA delivering under a lender's procurement and supervision regime, which is a precondition rather than proof of domestic capability. Building a powerhouse on an existing dam and tunnel is much less risky than a greenfield dam, which is part of why it came in on budget.

pattern.mechanism: WAPDA added generating capacity to an existing dam's spare tunnel under World Bank procurement and supervision, so the geological and resettlement risks that sink greenfield hydropower were mostly absent.
preconditions: An existing large dam with an unused tunnel and an operator that had run it for decades
Concessional finance with lender-imposed procurement, supervision and an independent panel of experts
A power deficit large enough that the plant was dispatched at once
pattern.travelled: Pakistan and the World Bank repeated the model at the same dam with the fifth extension (T5HP).

records.title: Ehsaas Emergency Cash
records.claim: Pakistan's government launched Ehsaas Emergency Cash in early April 2020 on BISP's existing payment and registry systems and had paid US$464 million to 6.4 million beneficiaries by 30 April 2020, reaching 15 million beneficiaries in all.

metric.name: Beneficiaries paid emergency cash by 30 April 2020, within about four weeks of launch

secondMetric.name: Beneficiaries given temporary income support through Ehsaas in 2020

source.publisher: World Bank, COVID-19 G2Px country brief: Pakistan

records.limits: Both figures are government-reported disbursement counts passed through World Bank documents, not independent verification that the money reached eligible families; the brief does not report inclusion or exclusion errors. The two World Bank documents disagree on the launch month (early April in the brief, March in the PAD) and do not reconcile the 15 million with the 12 million originally targeted. The transfer was one-off and small, about US$71 per family, so it shows speed of reconfiguration, not depth of protection. The speed rested on assets built over a decade (the BISP payment network and the national socio-economic registry), so the record evidences a programme being changed fast, which is the construct, but credits the 2020 government with infrastructure its predecessors built. The 'four weeks' is our reading of the brief's dates, not a published duration.

pattern.mechanism: The federal government raised the eligibility cutoff on an existing proxy-means-test registry, added an SMS application channel, and pushed one-off payments through BISP's contracted payment providers, so a new caseload was paid without building a new delivery system.
preconditions: A national socio-economic registry covering most households, with a proxy means score that could be re-cut
A biometric-verified payment network already contracted for a standing cash transfer
National ID and mobile coverage high enough for SMS self-registration

records.title: Italy's FinTech regulatory sandbox, and its contraction
records.claim: Italy's FinTech sandbox, run by the Bank of Italy, Consob and IVASS under the MEF's FinTech Committee, admitted 16 projects from its first application window (November 2021 to January 2022) but only 3 from its second (November to December 2023), after applications fell by about 80.7 percent.

metric.name: Projects admitted to the sandbox from the second application window (2 by IVASS, 1 by the Bank of Italy, 0 by Consob)

secondMetric.name: Projects admitted from the first application window, the peak (13 by the Bank of Italy, 3 by IVASS)

source.publisher: Ministry of Economy and Finance (Department of the Treasury), Relazione sulle attivita del Comitato FinTech 2023-2024

records.limits: The counts are projects, not firms: the IVASS projects in the second window involved several firms each (for example ITAS Mutua with ANIA, Autovia and Connexa InsTech), while the one Bank of Italy project was a single FinTech operator, so the indicator's firms-per-million figure would need a firm count the report does not give. Per million people the sandbox admitted roughly 0.27 projects from the first window and 0.05 from the second; those ratios are our computation with a population the source does not state. The sandbox runs in windows rather than continuously, so the two numbers are two cohorts, not two years. The MEF attributes the fall to an admission process that operators and the supervisors themselves found burdensome and to the Bank of Italy's informal channels (Canale Fintech, Milano Hub) absorbing demand, so part of the decline is innovation dialogue moving outside the sandbox, which the indicator would not see. The Bank of Italy's sandbox page shows both cohorts as concluded and lists no window after 2023 as of retrieval; a new window or a redesigned regime would change the status. The report is the MEF reporting on a regime it chairs, and the MEF itself judges the sandbox experience 'soddisfacente' while calling for procedural simplification.

pattern.mechanism: The MEF's FinTech Committee opened timed application windows in which each supervisor admitted projects to tests of six months, extendable to at most 18 months, with tailored conditions, and demand fell once operators learned how heavy admission was and found lighter informal channels at the Bank of Italy.
preconditions: A statutory sandbox shared across three supervisors with separate admission procedures
Lighter informal innovation channels at the central bank competing for the same applicants
Short, infrequent application windows that make the sandbox slow relative to product cycles

records.title: MOSE, the Venice lagoon flood barrier
records.claim: Works on MOSE, Italy's system of 78 mobile gates at Venice's three lagoon inlets, began in 2003. All the gates were first raised on 10 July 2020, and 6,689.07 million euros had been appropriated by mid-2022 with the works about 95 percent complete and still unfinished past their planned 2021 completion.

metric.name: Total funds appropriated for MOSE by the end of the first half of 2022

secondMetric.name: Share of the infrastructure completed at 17 June 2022, against a completion planned for 2021

source.publisher: Corte dei conti, Sezione centrale di controllo sulla gestione delle Amministrazioni dello Stato, deliberazione 92/2024/G (follow-up to deliberazione 35/2023/G)

records.limits: This is a delivery record with a bad cost and schedule history, not a success story: the barrier works, but late and expensive. The source gives total appropriations, not a baseline estimate, so a percentage overrun cannot be computed from it; the Court's report names a 'progressive increase in costs' without a starting figure here, and the original estimate quoted in the press is not used. Appropriated funds are not spending, and the total includes related works (Piano Europa, decarbonisation, San Marco basilica defences). The 95 percent completion figure is from June 2022 and the 2021 completion date had already passed; the record does not say when, or whether, the works were finished after that. The Court lists well-known judicial proceedings, a progressive increase in costs, technical difficulties, environmental questions and Covid-19 among the complexities of the build. The Court reports the gates have repeatedly protected the city, but the source gives no count of closures, so the record does not claim one.

pattern.mechanism: The state handed design and construction of the lagoon barrier to a single concessionaire consortium under a special law for Venice, and when delays and judicial proceedings stalled it, it appointed extraordinary commissioners to finish and operate the gates provisionally.
preconditions: A special legal regime and dedicated national funding for Venice dating from the 1980s
A single-concessionaire model that concentrated design, construction and control in one body
A visible, recurring flood threat that kept funding flowing through repeated delays

records.title: Fondo nuove competenze
records.claim: Italy's Fondo nuove competenze, set up in 2020 and run by the national labour policy agency ANPAL through two notices, was created to pay for working hours employers turned into training under union agreements, and by the end of 2021 it had covered almost 30 million hours of training for almost 270,000 workers, about 110 hours each.

metric.name: Workers trained under the first notice of the Fondo nuove competenze, per ANPAL's thematic review of 30 December 2021

secondMetric.name: Working hours converted to training

source.publisher: ANPAL, Agenzia Nazionale Politiche Attive del Lavoro (archive maintained by the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies)

records.limits: The figures come from ANPAL's own thematic review of December 2021, an interim count for the first notice; the final total for that edition is not on this page, and larger figures circulating elsewhere were not verified. The page is an archive: ANPAL was abolished and the fund passed to the Ministry of Labour, and the page says further funding is planned under the Programma nazionale Giovani, donne e lavoro. About 270,000 workers is under one percent of Italian adults (our rough computation), so this is a national programme that barely moves the participation share the indicator asks for. It is a wage subsidy as much as a training programme: the fund reimburses hours employers took out of production, and in 2020 to 2021 that also kept people employed during COVID restrictions. Training content and hours are certified by employers and union agreements, and ANPAL notes that the regions assessing training plans relied widely on tacit approval (silenzio-assenso), so quality control was light.

pattern.mechanism: ANPAL paid employers for working hours converted into training, but only where a collective agreement with the unions set out the cut in hours and the skills plan, which turned a COVID income measure into a negotiated training programme.
preconditions: A collective bargaining system able to sign thousands of firm-level agreements quickly
European Social Fund money to co-finance the wage cost
Regional bodies able to assess and certify training plans, even if mostly by tacit approval

records.title: National adult literacy projects of the Bureau of Non-Formal Education, and their erosion
records.claim: Bangladesh's Bureau of Non-Formal Education ran national adult literacy projects that reached 9.23 million learners aged 11 to 45 under the Total Literacy Movement project of 1997 to 2003, then 4.46 million aged 15 to 45 under the Basic Literacy Project (64 districts) of 2014 to 2022. Its only programme for learners above school age the bureau lists after June 2022 is a pre-vocational course that reached 4,198 people aged 14 to 24 in 2025-26.

metric.name: Learners reached, Basic Literacy Project (64 districts), Feb 2014 to Jun 2022

secondMetric.name: Peak: learners reached, Non-Formal Education Project-4 (Total Literacy Movement), Apr 1997 to Jun 2003

source.publisher: Bureau of Non-Formal Education, Ministry of Primary and Mass Education, Government of Bangladesh: implemented projects table

records.limits: These are the implementing bureau's own counts of learners it reports as reached. The page does not say how a learner was counted or whether literacy was tested. The numbers cover multi-year project windows and not the last 12 months, which is what the indicator asks. Spread over each window they are small against the adult population: roughly 0.5 million a year for 2014 to 2022 and 1.5 million a year for 1997 to 2003, both converted from lakh by us. The peak is itself a shortfall: the 1997 to 2003 project reached 92.25 lakh against a target of 228.89 lakh, about 40 percent. A hostile reviewer would say most of the fall reflects fewer illiterate adults to reach, since primary enrolment rose over the period, and not lost capacity. Nothing here measures that need, so the erosion is in delivery scale and not in a participation rate. The projects run as separate time-bound windows with gaps between them, so calling them one delivery is our reading. Both age bands include non-adults: the 1997 to 2003 project counted learners from age 11 and the 2014 to 2022 project from age 15, so part of each count is children and adolescents. The 2025-26 figure is a different course for ages 14 to 24 and is not a like-for-like successor. Basic Literacy Project teaching was contracted to NGOs. The page is a Bengali table on a government portal, and the values are read off its rows.

pattern.mechanism: The Bureau of Non-Formal Education used development-budget projects to fund literacy courses, delivered by district administrations or contracted NGOs, in every district. When a project window closed, delivery stopped until the next project was approved, and after 2022 no adult-scale successor followed.
preconditions: A standing bureau with a district presence to plan and monitor courses
Development-budget approval for each time-bound project, often with donor co-finance
NGOs or district administrations able to run community learning centres at scale
pattern.travelled: Time-bound literacy campaigns financed project by project were common across South Asia in the 1990s. The pattern they share is the one here: large one-off reach, then a gap when the project closes.

records.title: Cyclone Preparedness Programme
records.claim: Before Cyclone Remal made landfall on 26 May 2024, Bangladesh's government-run cyclone early warning and evacuation system moved about 0.8 million people into 9,424 evacuation shelters across 19 districts. The UN-coordinated response plan records 16 deaths among 4.6 million people affected.

metric.name: People pre-emptively evacuated to shelters ahead of Cyclone Remal landfall

secondMetric.name: Lives lost in Cyclone Remal (government assessment as reported in the plan)

source.publisher: UN Resident Coordinator's Office and Humanitarian Coordination Task Team, Bangladesh: Cyclone Remal Humanitarian Response Plan (June to December 2024)

records.limits: The evacuation and death figures are the government's own preliminary counts, repeated in a UN appeal document whose job is to raise funds. They are not an independent audit. The figures cover one cyclone, and Remal's death toll depended on its track, timing and surge as well as on preparedness. The plan credits the Cyclone Preparedness Programme with helping develop the warnings, but it does not attribute the evacuation to it alone: district administrations, shelters built under other programmes and anticipatory-action partners all took part. The plan states no baseline, so the record shows one storm's outcome and not a trend. The same document records 4.6 million people affected and 173,866 houses damaged or destroyed, so the system protected lives far more than it protected housing and livelihoods. The construct also covers recovery, which this number does not show. The figure sits inside a PDF.

pattern.mechanism: The government took over the cost of a Red Crescent volunteer warning network in 1973 and ran it jointly with the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society. Village volunteers relay meteorological department signals door to door and move people into shelters before landfall.
preconditions: A meteorological service able to issue track forecasts days ahead of landfall
A shelter stock within walking distance of exposed coastal villages
A volunteer corps, trained and equipped, kept active in years without a major storm
pattern.travelled: The volunteer-relay model shaped community early warning in Odisha and Myanmar. Copies tend to keep the sirens and drop the standing volunteer corps, which is the part that turns a warning into an evacuation.

records.title: Padma Multipurpose Bridge
records.claim: Bangladesh's Bridge Authority completed the 6.15 km Padma road-rail bridge with government funds. It opened to traffic on 26 June 2022 at a reported actual cost of Tk 30,770 crore, six and a half years after the 31 December 2015 completion date in the 2010 Asian Development Bank appraisal, which had costed the project at $2,915 million.

metric.name: Actual project cost reported by the Bangladesh Bridge Authority

secondMetric.name: Appraised total project cost and completion date, ADB Report and Recommendation of the President (completion 31 Dec 2015)

source.publisher: Bangladesh Bridge Authority, Bridges Division, Ministry of Road Transport and Bridges: Padma Bridge project page

records.limits: Neither source publishes an overrun percentage. Converting the ADB appraisal at the RRP's own rate of Tk 70.11 per dollar gives about Tk 20,440 crore, so the actual cost is about 51 percent higher. That figure is our computation, and it mixes a 2010 dollar estimate with a taka outturn after more than a decade of taka depreciation and inflation, so much of the gap is currency and price level, not overrun. The ADB estimate includes $99 million of financing charges and appraised a co-financed project. The bridge was built with government funds, as the Bridge Authority page states, after that financing structure changed, so the two figures do not describe the same contract package. Against the government's own revised estimates on the same page, the outturn is about 5 percent below the Tk 32,306 crore figure and about 2 percent above the Tk 30,193 crore figure, which is why the cost record depends on which baseline is chosen. The Bridge Authority page is itself inconsistent: it lists two different estimates under the third revised project document. The schedule slip is clearer: an appraised completion of December 2015 against road opening in June 2022 and project closure in June 2024. The started year is the project start the Bridge Authority states, before main construction contracts were let.
